Thus, when we contemplate the Prophet, peace be upon him, treating the diseases of souls, when a young man from among the Bedouins who had believed came to him complaining of his weakness before women and his lack of patience against this desire, to the point that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to commit fornication," yet the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, did not rebuke him. Rather, he knew that he was before a sick person who needed someone to treat him and to draw out from his soul this unbridled upheaval, especially since he had been frank with the Messenger of Allah about what he suffered, so he was honest with himself and did not deceive it.

Therefore the Messenger of Allah brought him near and said: "O brother of the Arabs, would you like this for your mother? Would you like this for your wife? Would you like this for your sister? Would you like this for your daughter?" And the young man, in all of this, kept saying: "No, O Messenger of Allah, may I be your ransom."

Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: ((Likewise, people, O brother of the Arabs, do not like this for their mothers, nor for their wives, nor for their sisters, nor for their daughters.))(3)

The young man left, saying: "By Allah, nothing is more hateful to me than fornication after what I have heard from the Messenger of Allah, and whenever desire came upon me, I remembered the Messenger of Allah's words about my mother, my wife, my sister, and my daughter."

What emboldens people to disobedience and to being addicted to it is the absence of keeping the punishment in mind and not considering the consequences; similarly, they become disinclined to obedience because they do not keep its reward in mind.

We have previously said to university students: Suppose a youth has a sexual appetite; he is an unrestrained appetite that wants to satisfy his lust in what is forbidden, and we want him to repent. We told him: "We will provide what you desire on condition that you throw yourself into this (furnace) after you spend your night as you like." What does he do?

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Qasas]. And in other places: ﴿Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [al-Ma'idah 108], ﴿Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah 264], and all of these indicate that Allah does not withhold guidance from anyone except because of something that preceded from him. The guidance meant here is the guidance of faith and piety; otherwise Allah has guided everyone with the guidance of indication and direction, but these people did not take it, so they were deprived of the guidance of faith.

1 Narrated by Ibn Abi 'Asim in *Kitab as-Sunnah* (1/12) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As. Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali cited it in *Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam* (p. 460) and declared it weak.
2 Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi is Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Kindi, the wise poet and one of the glories of Arabic literature, author of widely circulated proverbs and profound maxims. Born in Kufa in 303 AH in a quarter called "Kinda," he grew up in Syria, claimed prophethood in the Samawa desert, and was killed in 354 AH by a group who rebelled against him on the road. [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 1/115].
3 From Abu Umamah: a man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to commit fornication." Those near the Prophet, peace be upon him, moved to seize him, but the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Leave him." Then he said to him: "Would you like this to be done to your sister?" He said: "No." He said: "Your daughter?" He said: "No." He kept saying "[would you like it for] so-and-so, [so-and-so]," and each time he said: "No." Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Hate what Allah hates, and love for your brother what you love for yourself." Cited by al-Muttaqi al-Hindi in *Muntakhab Kanz al-'Ummal* (2/397), attributing it to Ibn Jarir al-Tabari.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word, that they might remember.﴾ [28:51]

The word ﴿وصلنا﴾ (wassalna, "We have conveyed/caused to arrive in sequence") suggests things that have been separated from one another, and we wish to join them together. So His saying, ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word, that they might remember⁠﴾ [28:51] means: We conveyed to them the messages. Whenever the era of one messenger passed and the people disbelieved, Allah brought them another message, so that creation would remain connected to the guidance of the Creator and to His method. Or: the matter is specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the meaning is that We conveyed to him the verses, so that whenever a portion (najm) of the Qur'an was revealed to him, We connected it to another portion according to events.

For this reason, this issue was among the objections raised by the opponents of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when they said, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?"⁠﴾ [25:32]. The Qur'an responded to them to explain to them the wisdom of its being revealed in portions (munajjaman): ﴿Thus [it is], that We may strengthen thereby your heart, and We have spaced it out distinctly⁠﴾ [25:32].

Had the Qur'an been revealed all at once, the strengthening would have been given to the Messenger of Allah only one time, whereas he needed continuous strengthening along with the events he would encounter. So Allah conveys the verses to him so that he remains mindful of hearing the words of his Lord whenever events grow severe for him; a portion of the Qur'an comes to him to console him and to relieve him of what he encounters from his opponents.

Another wisdom is in His saying: ﴿and We have spaced it out distinctly⁠﴾ [25:32] (wa-rattalnahu tartila, "We have recited it in distinct measure"). Whenever a portion of the Qur'an was revealed, it became easy for them to memorize it, arrange it, and act upon it. Likewise, the believers who were commanded with this method would face issues, and they would ask the Messenger of Allah about them; how would the answer be given to them if the Qur'an had been revealed all at once?

The answer must be delayed until the question arises; therefore He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they bring you no example but that We bring you the truth and the best explanation⁠﴾ [25:33].

The verb "they ask you" (yas'alunaka) occurs in the Qur'an several times in various surahs. How could the answer be given to us if the Qur'an had come all at once, as you say? Then, glory be to Allah, have you been able to bear it in portions, that you would demand it all at once?

Then the verse concludes with another wisdom: ﴿that they might remember⁠﴾ [28:51]. Whenever a portion of the Qur'an was revealed, it reminded them of what they had neglected of Allah's method.

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it.﴾

It is as if Allah, blessed and exalted is He, is saying to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "I will make your opponents among the People of the Book the ones who bear witness to your truthfulness, because they know you as they know their own sons, and what came in your Book is mentioned in their books, and your likeness and attributes are described among them."

Therefore you find many verses of the Book of Allah relying on the People of the Book for knowledge of the truth that the Qur'an brought. He, exalted is He, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and [so is] whoever has knowledge of the Book."﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 43]

They too are witnesses to the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah by what they have of the earlier scriptures, so ask them.

And He, exalted is He, says:

﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring. Indeed, this is in the former scrolls, the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.﴾ [Al-A'la: 16–19]

And the Almighty says:

﴿And among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah.﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 199]

And otherwise, why did 'Abdullah ibn Salam and other scholars of the Jews embrace Islam?

So then: the People of the Book who are truthful with themselves and with their Books must believe in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). As for those who did not believe, they were blinded by temporal authority and the eagerness for the sovereignty they had held before Islam: sovereignty in knowledge, in war, and in wealth.

Among these was 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and the people of Madinah were preparing to crown him king over them. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emigrated to it, he spoiled for them what they wanted and stripped them of this sovereignty. Temporal authority, when it interferes, means that people's desires become involved, so they use the purposes of Allah in the service of their desires, rather than serving the purposes of Allah.

Then the Exalted says:

{And when it is recited to them, they say: "We have believed in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it."}

These believers from the People of the Book, when the Qur'an is recited to them, say: "We have believed in it," and they testify that it is the truth from Allah, and that they did not increase in faith by hearing its verses. They were Muslims before it, for they had first believed in their own scriptures, and likewise they believed in the Qur'an.

(1) Occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of the verse: Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, Tamim al-Dari, al-Jarud al-'Abdi and Salman al-Farisi; they embraced Islam, and this verse was revealed about them. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/5183] Al-Qurtubi said: it also includes those among the Christian scholars who embraced Islam, who were forty men who came to Madinah with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib: thirty-two men from Abyssinia and eight persons who came from al-Sham, and they were leaders of the Christians, among them Bahira the monk, Abraha, al-Ashraf, 'Amir, Ayman, Idris and Nafi'. Thus al-Mawardi named them.

The Exalted wishes to teach us that whoever seeks a true religion must look to a religion that comes after it with a miracle. For if he believed when Jesus came that he came after Moses, peace be upon them, then it is not unreasonable by reason that a messenger should come after Jesus. Therefore it is obligatory upon him to investigate the new religion and to examine the proofs that justify his belief in this religion.

Here, if the first religion has not changed, [the matter is as above]; but if the first religion has been altered, the matter is clear, for alteration creates a gap for one who seeks a religion: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the unlettered, whom they find written with them in the Torah...﴾ [al-A'raf 7:157]

They believed in him because they found his description, and they found the creeds that do not change present in his book, while he was unlettered and knew nothing of this; so they took his unlettered state as evidence of his truthfulness.

As for His saying, ﴿Those...﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54], it means: the People of the Book who believe in the Qur'an while they are humbly submissive to God, and who were described earlier. ﴿They will be given their reward twice, for that they were patient﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54]: a reward for their belief in their messengers, and a reward for their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Thus there came in the noble hadith: "Three will be given their reward twice: a man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and then believed in me; a slave who fulfilled the right of God and the right of his masters; and a man who had a slave-girl (jariyah), whom he disciplined and educated well, then freed her and married her."(1)

Those who believed in their messengers and then believed in the Messenger of God earned this rank and obtained these two rewards, because they were subjected to harm from those who had not believed in the first faith, and then they were subjected to harm in the second faith, and they endured both harms. This is the reason for ﴿they will be given their reward twice, for that they were patient﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54].

Just as God gives the People of the Book who believed in Muhammad their reward twice, so He gives some Muslims their reward twice, and among them, as our master the Messenger of God explained: "a slave who fulfilled the right of God and the right of his masters, and a man who had a slave-girl..."

This reward is not denied to the religion that directly preceded Islam and came before it, namely Christianity; so they too have this, and therefore God says:

﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for people...﴾ [al-Hadid 57:25]

The most important of these benefits is ﴿that God may know who helps Him and His messengers in the unseen﴾ [al-Hadid 57:25]. He mentioned iron because weapons of war are made from it.

So: God sent down the Qur'an for one task and sent down iron for another task; therefore the poet says:

"Nothing but revelation, or a sharp edge
that straightens the necks (akhda') of every deviant.
This is the remedy for the disease of every sensible person,
and that is the remedy for the disease of every ignorant person."

I myself have memories and situations with this verse, ﴿They will be given their reward twice, for that they were patient﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54]. We were once in a country where there were some of our Christian brothers, and among them was a man of intellect and thought, who always consoled the Muslims, attended their funerals and listened to the Qur'an, and some verses clung to his mind. He came to me once saying: "I heard the reciter read: ﴿We sent you not but as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:107]. Are we not among the worlds?" I said to him: "Yes, Muhammad was sent as a mercy to all the worlds; whoever believes in him attains his mercy, and whoever does not believe in him is deprived of it. Nevertheless, if you look at the Qur'an with careful and insightful contemplation, you will find that it shows mercy to the non-believer." He said: "How?" So I recited to him His saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between people by what God has shown you, and do not be a advocate for the treacherous﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:105]. It did not say "between the believers." ﴿And seek forgiveness of God; indeed God is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:106]; for God does not love the treacherous sinner, even if he is a Muslim.

Then I mentioned to him the occasion of revelation of this verse, which is the story of the coat of mail that the Jew Zayd ibn al-Sammin deposited as a trust with Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, the Muslim. The coat of mail had been stolen from Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man. When Qatadah missed it, he went to search for it; he had placed it in a bag of flour, so he followed the trail of the flour until it led to the house of the Jew Zayd ibn al-Sammin, and he accused him of the theft and spread the matter among the people. The Jew then related what had happened with Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, and that he had deposited the coat of mail with him as a trust, because he feared it would be stolen from his house.

Here the Muslims wished to clear their companion, because he was recently converted, and how would their image look if it spread among people that one of them was a thief? They inclined to condemn the Jews, and indeed they presented this view to the Messenger of God so that he might find in it a solution that would extricate them from this predicament, even though they did not rule out that Ibn Ubayriq had stolen.

The Messenger of God sat pondering this matter, but soon revelation came down to him, saying: this matter does not require thought or investigation: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:105].

The verse condemned Ibn Ubayriq and showed that this was not the first incident concerning him; it described him as a khawwan, that is, one who frequently betrays, and it exonerated the Jew, and corrected the view of the Muslims who feared the disgrace of a Muslim being a thief, and who overlooked the bad effect of reversing the facts and condemning the Jew.

Thus the verse, although it condemned the Muslim, raised the standing of Islam in the eyes of everyone: the Muslim, the Jew, and everyone who lived through this story, and indeed everyone who reads this verse. Had the Messenger of God inclined and shown partiality to the Muslim, the image of Islam would have been shaken in the eyes of all. And had this happened, what would have been the stance of the Jews who were drawn to Islam, and who in fact did embrace Islam after what occurred?

This matter resembles the false witness, who is the first to fall from the esteem of the one in whose favour he testified, so that they say: "Whoever makes you a place of blame has fallen from his regard; even if you assist him in his affair, a false witness raises your head over the opponent by his testimony, while your foot treads upon his dignity."

As for His saying: ﴿and they repel evil with good﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54], this is also among their qualities: they repel evil with good. Among their attributes is pardon and forgiveness, as God says: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, that is indeed of the matters requiring resolve﴾ [al-Shura 42:43]. ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [al-Qasas 28:54]: the obligatory spending upon oneself and one's family, and the obligatory spending for the poor, which is zakat, then the voluntary spending for the needy and those in want.

1 Hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayhi). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (97), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (154), Kitab al-Iman, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with him, in similar wording.
2 al-Zaba: the edge of a sword, spear, blade, dagger, and the like. [Lisan al-Arab, root: z-b-a]
3 al-Akhda'an: two veins on either side of the neck that are hidden and deep. al-Lihyani said: they are two veins in the neck. [Lisan al-Arab, root: kh-d-']
4 Cited by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 103), Al-Maktabah al-Thaqafiyyah edition, Beirut.
5 Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani said in al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah (3/285) (biography 4238): "Abu Ishaq al-Mustalmi mentioned him among the Companions and said: he attended all the battles except Badr... and the faith of Tu'mah has been spoken of."

This is another attribute of the believers: ﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it...﴾ [Al-Qasas]. Al-lagha (vain talk) is speech that has no benefit in it: it does not help you if you hear it, and not hearing it does not harm you. The intelligent person should leave it, for it deserves to be abandoned and disregarded.

For this reason, among the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful is: ﴿And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [Al-Furqan], i.e., they do not turn their attention to it.

The occasion of revelation of this verse(1): When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met the envoys of al-Najashi, who were a group of priests (qissisun), once they sat down he recited to them Surah Ya-Sin, and they were affected by it until they all wept. Then they believed in the Messenger of Allah. When they departed, Abu Jahl confronted them, rebuked them, and said: "May Allah disappoint you, O caravan" – they were a group coming on a mission – "sent by someone behind me" – meaning al-Najashi – "to learn for him the news of this man, and you heard him, wept, and embraced Islam. By Allah, we have never seen a more foolish caravan than you." So they turned away from him.

This is the meaning of the word of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds..."﴾ [Al-Qasas]

These men passed by vain talk with dignity, turned away from it, and did not turn their attention to it. They went further than that: they did not remain silent in the face of vain talk, but said: ﴿"To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant."﴾ [Al-Qasas] "To us our good deeds, which we must devote ourselves to, and to you your false deeds, which should be abandoned; each of us has a matter that occupies him."

﴿"Peace be upon you..."﴾ [Al-Qasas] Peace (salam) is either a greeting of peace, as is common among us, or a peace of parting (salam al-mutaraka), as when you have entered into a dispute with your companion, and when you see that it will be prolonged and perhaps you will exceed bounds with him, you say to him, leaving: "Peace be upon you," meaning: "I have nothing more to say to part from you except this word."

Among this is what passed between the Friend, Ibrahim (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet), and his uncle: after he debated with him and reached no result, he said to him: ﴿"Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you..."﴾ [Maryam]

(1) Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as related by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/393), and said by 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, as transmitted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5183). Ibn Kathir attributed the story to Muhammad ibn Ishaq in the Sira.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.﴾

This address to our master, the Messenger of Allah, is specific to his call to his uncle Abu Talib, who remained upon the religion of his people. However, he protected the Messenger of Allah out of tribal loyalty and family ties, not out of love for Islam. Allah the Exalted has a wisdom in Abu Talib remaining upon disbelief, because by that he gained the favour of the Quraysh and earned their respect. They were pleased that he did not believe in Muhammad and did not show him courtesy, and they were pleased that he remained upon the religion of the forefathers, so they respected his protection of his nephew. This prevented the Messenger of Allah from their harm, and protected the call from many of the assaults upon him. Therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was eager to repay this kindness. Yet repaying a kindness does not come through a worldly possession; rather, through something lasting and everlasting. So when death approached Abu Talib, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: ((O uncle, say: there is no god but Allah, a word by which I may intercede for you on the Day of Resurrection)). He said: "O son of my brother, were it not that the Quraysh would reproach me for this matter, saying that he only accepted faith out of fear of death, I would have gladdened your eye by it."

However, it is narrated that after Abu Talib passed away, al-Abbas came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him: "O Muhammad, the word you asked your uncle to say, he said it before he died, and I bear witness to it."

We note here the precision of expression from al-Abbas: he did not say "this word is there is no god but Allah," but called it (the word). Why? Because he had not yet embraced Islam.

We have previously discussed the meaning of guidance (hidayah) in ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like...﴾ [al-Qasas: 56], and we said that it comes in one of two meanings: the meaning of direction and indication (irshad wa dalalah), and the meaning of assistance granted to one who believes upon the indication. Among that is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17], i.e., they heard the indication and obeyed it, so Allah increased them in another guidance, which is the guidance of faith and assistance.

Allah the Exalted says on this matter: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾ [Fussilat: 17], meaning: We indicated to them, ﴿but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17]; therefore they were deprived of the guidance of assistance.

So then: the guidance negated from our master, the Messenger of Allah, in ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like...﴾ [al-Qasas: 56], is the guidance of assistance and the granting of success to faith, because he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, guided everyone with the guidance of indication and direction; and among what he said was: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [as-Saff: 10]. So the guidance of indication originated first from Allah the Exalted, then through the conveyance by His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, secondly.

1 Occasion of revelation of the verse: Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: The exegetes unanimously agreed that it was revealed concerning Abu Talib. Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 194).
And Ibn Abbas said it (narrated by Ibn Mardawayh), and Ibn Umar (narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, and Abu Dawud in al-Qadar), and Qatadah (narrated by Abd ibn Humayd). Al-Suyuti cited all these statements in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/429).
2 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (25), Book of Faith, and by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/344), and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 194, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 28, verse 57:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{And they said, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched away from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which the fruits of all things are brought as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.} (57)

This statement, ﴿If we follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched away from our land...﴾ (28:57), was said by al-Harith ibn Uthman ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf. He went to our master, the Messenger of Allah, and said: "We know that you have brought the truth, but we fear that if we believe in you and follow your way, we will be snatched away from our land." He must have been speaking in the language of his people, who had agreed upon this statement.

Al-khatf (snatching) is: taking by force and speed.

So they acknowledge to the Messenger that he has brought the truth and that he is upon guidance, but the cause of their refusal is that they would be snatched away. They should have compared, with their intellects, between being with the Messenger of Allah upon truth and guidance and being snatched away, and between remaining in their disbelief.

The most that can befall them if they follow the Messenger of Allah is that people snatch them away in their wealth or in their persons, on the supposition that this is true. The most that befalls them is the loss of a worldly benefit, for whatever of this world you would have enjoyed would have been enjoyed for the duration of your stay in it. This good of the world that you would miss is limited by the measure of human power, and this will not harm you if you are among the people of the Hereafter, since there will go to you a good that is lasting and eternal, a good that befits the power of the Benefactor, glorified is He.

As for if they remain in their disbelief, it is a little enjoyment in the transient world, and they have no share in the everlasting Hereafter. So, which path is more rightly guided? Rational comparison favours the path of guidance and following the truth which the Messenger of Allah brought. This is the first point.

Then, who said that if you follow the guidance with the Messenger of Allah you will be snatched away and persecuted? Therefore, Allah responds to them: Say to them, O Muhammad: You have lied; none will snatch you away because of your Islam. ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which the fruits of all things are brought as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.﴾ (28:57)

Allah has bestowed favour upon you while you were disbelievers, associating others with Him, worshipping idols in ignorance. He established for you a secure life within the precincts of His Sacred House, and provided you with abundant living, while you were in a valley without cultivation, where fruits are brought to it from every place. So the One who did this for you, will He abandon you and forsake you after you have believed in Him and been guided to the truth? How can you make such an analogy?

The meaning of ﴿Have We not established for them...﴾ (28:57) is an interrogative for affirmation. Ask them, and they will acknowledge that Allah has established for them a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of all things are brought. Thus the Truth, glorified is He, wishes to establish this matter through their own acknowledgment of it.

The meaning of ﴿We establish for them...﴾ (28:57) is: We make them firmly established in it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus did We establish Joseph in the land...﴾ (12:21). Establishment (al-tamkin) indicates stability, because the spatial container (ẓarf al-makan) is stable, unlike the temporal container (ẓarf al-zaman).

He said ﴿a secure sanctuary﴾ (28:57), although security belongs to those who are in the place. But He, glorified is He, wished to make the place itself secure, so that everything in it is secure: even the killer is not to be retaliated against within the Sanctuary, the animal is not to be pursued or hunted in it, the plants are not to be cut, and even the stone in this place is secure. Do you not see them throwing stones in the stoning of the pillars (jamarat), while they honour the Black Stone and kiss it?

When we reflect upon the Sanctuary from the days of the Friend, Abraham, peace be upon him, we find that it has a plan, and that the Truth, glorified is He, was preparing it to be a secure sanctuary. When Abraham came to it he said: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House...﴾ (14:37)

This means that the place has none of the requisites of life except air, because the negation of cultivation means the absence of water. Therefore Hajar objected to this barren place, but when she learned that it was Allah's choice for them she said: "Then He will not abandon us." (1)

She saw with her own eyes that Allah had not abandoned them. When her child needed water to suckle, she strove to seek it between al-Safa and al-Marwa, seven circuits, as much as she could bear, and she did not find water in her striving. Had she found it, her striving would have been a cause. Allah wished to confirm her word and to show her that He, glorified is He, would not abandon them without means, to affirm that her word was true. Then the power of Allah willed that water should gush out from beneath the foot of the infant, as he struck the ground with his foot, weeping from the intensity of hunger and thirst, and Zamzam burst forth.

When Abraham settled his family in this barren place, he intended it for them as a permanent dwelling, not merely a rest from the hardship of travel. Therefore he said: ﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer; so make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them of the fruits...﴾ (14:37)

It is as if he, peace be upon him, wished to be assured of his family's settlement in this place, and that the House should be a place of worship for Allah, where prayer is never interrupted. This is the difference between the House of Allah chosen by Allah and a house chosen by the servants of Allah.

The house we build for Allah, exalted is He, may be closed even at the times of the obligatory prayers, but the House of Allah which He took for Himself is never without circumambulation (tawaf) and prayer at any time of night or day. Circumambulation does not cease there except for the prescribed prayer, and when the prayer is finished you see people hastening to circumambulate.

I saw the Sanctuary in one of the years when a violent flood overwhelmed it, until it filled its courtyard, and water entered the Ka'bah and covered the Black Stone, so people were circumambulating by swimming, and we saw people diving at the Stone to kiss it. It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wishes that the circumambulation around His House should not cease under any circumstance.

Likewise we understand from His saying ﴿...that they may incline toward them...﴾ (14:37), from the verb hawa, yahwi, meaning: to fall, because one who falls has no will to avoid falling. Likewise, whoever comes to the House of Allah or has good things brought to it finds a driving force that drives him, as if he had no will of his own.

We also understand from it another meaning: all the obligations of the Truth, glorified is He, people may be lax in performing them. Some do not pray or do not pay zakat, except for the Hajj, concerning which Allah said: ﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot...﴾ (22:27). Merely by your announcing, they come to you.

Therefore you find, among those unable to afford the expenses of Hajj, someone who goes hungry and withholds from his family in order to save the cost of Hajj. It is therefore the only obligation for which people rush, though it has not been demanded of them.

We also note that Abraham, peace be upon him, invoked security for the Sanctuary twice. Once in His saying: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure land...﴾ (2:126), meaning: make this place a secure land, like any secure land, which is not established except in a place where all the requisites of life are secure for them. Any land, even one built by a disbeliever, is not built except where it is secure. So the first request was that this empty place be transformed into a secure land, as every land is secure when it comes into being. This is general security.

Then he invoked again: ﴿My Lord, make this city secure...﴾ (14:35), after Makkah had become a secure land, asking for it further security. This is special security, as He made it a sacred territory (haram), where human, animal and plant, and even inanimate things, are secure.

Some have paused at His saying:

﴿And whoever enters it is secure...﴾ (3:97)

and said: where is this security, when aggression and killing and the terrorising of the secure have occurred in the Sanctuary, as happened in the days of the Qaramita when they entered the Sanctuary, killed people in it, and took the Stone; and in modern times we know the story of Juhayman, and the killing that occurred in it within the Sanctuary.

This verse, ﴿And whoever enters it is secure﴾ (3:97), is a declarative sentence whose purpose is command and exhortation, as if He, exalted is He, had said: Make secure whoever enters the Sanctuary. This is not a cosmic (kawni) matter but a legislative (shar'i) one, and there is a difference between the two matters: the cosmic must occur, whereas the legislative is a command that some carry out and some rebel against. So whoever obeys the legislative command of Allah and wishes to make Allah's command true secures the people of the Sanctuary, and whoever wishes to contradict his Lord agitates and terrorises the people in it.

Among the verses frequently asked about in this regard is His saying: ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women; and good women are for good men, and good men for good women...﴾ (24:26). They say: a wicked man often marries a good woman, or a good woman a wicked man, so reality does not accord with the verse. We say here too: this is a legislative matter carrying a command which may be obeyed or disobeyed, and not a cosmic matter that must come to pass as Allah informed, nor does its meaning fail to hold.

So the meaning of the verse is: if you marry, then marry the wicked to the wicked woman, and the good to the good woman, so that compatibility between the spouses is realised and harmony arises between them; so that if the wicked man reproaches his wife, she would be like him and able to answer him back. There must be equivalence even in ugliness; otherwise how would a good woman fare with a wicked man, or a wicked man with a good woman?

Therefore, the verse and its like are a legislative matter in the form of a statement, though they mean a command, just as you say of the dead: "May Allah have mercy on him," in the past tense, though you do not know whether Allah has had mercy on him or not. So the meaning must be a supplication: "May Allah have mercy on him," you say in the past tense, hoping that mercy will be his.

Returning to His saying: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary...﴾ (28:57), we note this establishment and this security in the story of the Elephant, when Abrahah came to demolish the Ka'bah, and the army advanced with a huge elephant called Mahmud. When they said into its ear, "Kneel down, Mahmud, and turn back in safety" (1)—meaning, "escape with your skin, for you are in the land of Allah, the Sacred" — the elephant knelt down and complied.

Then came the battle of the birds (al-tayr al-ababil), pelting them with stones of sijjil, so He made them like chewed-up stalks. All of this is part of the security which Allah granted to Quraysh, the inhabitants of His Sanctuary, so that the Ka'bah would remain inhabited by them. As long as they are the inhabitants of the Sanctuary, and people come to them from all directions for the Hajj every year, security will remain theirs among the tribes, and no one will dare to attack them or interfere with their caravans on their journeys in winter and summer. What security, and what dignity, after this!

Along with the pilgrims, food is brought and provisions are brought, and the Great God spoke truly: ﴿For the familiarity of the Quraysh, their familiarity with the caravan of winter and summer, let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear.﴾ (106:1–4)

And how, after this security and safety, could one who believes in Muhammad fear being snatched away from his land? It is a statement with no meaning.

(1) Occasion of revelation: al-Wahidi said in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 194): "It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Uthman ibn Abd Manaf, for he said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: 'We know that what you say is true, but what prevents us from following you is that the Arabs would snatch us from our land, since they are united against us and we have no power against them.' So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse." This was reported from Ibn Abbas, as cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5186).

(2) Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3364) from a hadith of Ibn Abbas, a long hadith, in which Abraham brought Hajar and her son Isma'il, while she was nursing him, and placed them at the House, by a tree above Zamzam, at the top of the mosque. There was no one in Makkah at that time, and there was no water there, so he placed them there and left with them a bag containing dates and a waterskin containing water. Then Abraham set off, and Isma'il's mother followed him, saying: "O Abraham, where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no person or anything?" She said this to him many times, but he did not turn to her. She said: "Did Allah command you to do this?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Then He will not abandon us."

(3) Cited by Ibn Hisham in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (1/52). The one who said to the elephant, "Kneel," was Nufayl ibn Habib al-Khath'ami. In it: they struck the elephant to make it rise, but it refused; they struck it on its head with a tabarzin to make it rise, but it refused; they inserted their hooked staffs (mahajin; a stick with a bent head) into its flanks to make it rise, but it refused; they turned it back toward Yemen, and it rose and trotted; they turned it toward Syria and it did the same; they turned it toward the east and it did the same; they turned it toward Makkah, and it knelt down.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 28, verse 58:

The word ﴿وكم﴾ [al-Qasas]: here "kam" is khabariyya (a numerative "kam" expressing a great quantity). It is as though you have left out the answer so that it indicates the abundance by itself, just as you say to someone who denies your favour, and you do not want to enumerate your kindnesses to him: "How much I have done good to you!" meaning: "I will not enumerate, and I will be content with whatever you say, because you are confident that the answer will be in your favour." At that point he can only say, "Yes, it is many." So "kam" here means abundance, and the addressee pronounces it himself so that it becomes a proof against him.

As for the meaning of ﴿من قرية﴾ [al-Qasas]: "min" is for generality, i.e., from the beginning of whatever is called a "qarya" (town/community). ﴿بطرت معيشتها﴾ [al-Qasas]: al-batar (insolence in favour) is to forget to thank the Benefactor for His blessings, meaning that He, glory be to Him, has not been remembered in your mind while you revel in His blessings; or batar is using the blessing in disobedience to the Benefactor, mighty and majestic.

Among batar is that a person rises above a blessing, or considers it little and regards it as below his level, like the child to whom his mother brings, for example, a plate of lentils, and he grumbles about it and perhaps does not eat it; so the mother says, as we say in colloquial speech: "Are you being insolent (bitbattar) toward the blessing of our Lord?" A word in our colloquial language, but it has a root in classical Arabic (al-fuṣḥā).

So, from batar is that you become arrogant, or haughty, or exalt yourself over the blessing of God, so you are not content with it, and you seek something higher than it.

As for the meaning of ﴿معيشتها﴾ [al-Qasas]: i.e., the means of its livelihood. ﴿فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين﴾ [al-Qasas]: since they insolently rejected God's blessing, it is necessary that He strip it from their hands; and if the blessings of God are removed from a land, they perish or depart from it. ﴿إلا قليلا﴾ [al-Qasas]: these are the ones who remain after the destruction of their dwellings.

﴿وكنا نحن الوارثين﴾ [al-Qasas]: We inherit them because they left no one to inherit from them, and when a place is left without a successor, its inheritance returns to God, exalted is He.

In another verse, the Truth, glory be to Him, treats this matter in a broader manner. He says: ﴿وضرب الله مثلا قرية كانت آمنة مطمئنة يأتيها رزقها رغدا من كل مكان فكفرت بأنعم الله..﴾ [an-Nahl, 112], meaning: they were insolent with His blessings, may He be exalted. ﴿فأذاقها الله لباس الجوع والخوف..﴾ [an-Nahl, 112].

The meaning of disbelief (kufr) in God is: concealing the existence of God. Concealment requires something concealed, so the original state is that God, exalted is He, exists, but the disbeliever conceals this existence. Thus disbelief itself becomes evidence of faith, since faith is the original and disbelief is something that occurs upon it.

An example of this is our saying: falsehood is a soldier of the soldiers of truth. When falsehood spreads and people taste its bitterness and are burned by its fire, they return to the truth and to what is right, and they seek the way out in it when events beset them.

Likewise we say by the same logic: pain is the first soldier of healing. Therefore we find that the most dangerous diseases are those that creep upon the patient without making him feel any pain, so that he does not know of it except when its affair has grown severe, its danger has multiplied, and its cure has become difficult; therefore we call it, God forbid, the "wicked disease."

In His saying: ﴿فكفرت بأنعم الله..﴾ [an-Nahl, 112] is evidence of the existence of blessings, yet they disbelieved in them, i.e., concealed them, either by not investigating their causes and being lax in extracting them, or by concealing them from those who deserve them and withholding them from the incapable who cannot earn; therefore God strips them of these blessings and deprives them of them despite their ability.

There are things which, if they remained present, would produce monotony, so that they might understand that these things come to them automatically by the nature of things. When God takes away His blessings from them and cuts this monotony, it is so that they understand that monotony in obligations weakens the wisdom of the obligation. How?

We say: the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has forbidden us some things and permitted us others. For example, God forbade us wine until we no longer drink it and it does not even occur to our minds, and it became a routine habit with us. God, exalted is He, wants to keep the obligation of worship upon man, so that he does not become accustomed to it and perform it out of habit; so He breaks this habit, for example, in the fasting of Ramadan.

He forbids you what was lawful for you all year, to which you had become accustomed; then Ramadan comes and the obligation of fasting forbids you the food you were eating yesterday. This is so that the warmth of worship remains present, drawing the servant toward it and training him in discipline in performing obligations.

Then He mentions the punishment for disbelief in God's blessing: ﴿فأذاقها الله لباس الجوع والخوف..﴾ [an-Nahl, 112]. Hunger has two aspects: first, the belly demands it; then if hunger increases, the limbs weaken, all the organs are pained, and they taste the pain of hunger. God, exalted is He, wants to show us the comprehensiveness of this pain, so He likened it to a garment that encompasses the whole body and wraps it on all sides.

Such is the way of God with the unjust towns, as He, glorified is He, said:

{And your Lord would never destroy the towns until He had sent to their mother-town a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We never destroy the towns unless their people are wrongdoers.} [28:59]

So: there must be a clear method, and a messenger must come saying, "Do this, and do not do that," so that when punishment descends upon the disbelievers it comes with justice, after the proof has been established against them. It is not that we leave people to sin and then tell them, "This is forbidden."

We have already mentioned what the law says: there is no punishment except through prohibition, no criminalization except through explicit text, and no text except through notification. God would not destroy a town unjustly; rather, it is a punishment for them for what they did.

The word "qarya" (town) has a sequence. We say: "najε" (naj' — a hamlet, the place inhabited by a single family), then "kafr" (kafr — a settlement of several families), then "qarya" (qarya — a village/town), then "umm al-qura" (umm al-qura — the mother of towns), which is the capital or the main city. The Qur'an was revealed to a nomadic nation that lived by wandering and dwelt in tents, moving between pastures; so they called "umm al-qura" the place where towns are found and where the necessities of life are available in a way not found in the hamlets, the kafrs, and the small villages. Just as the people of the countryside now rely on the "bandar" (bandar — the town market/city) to meet their needs, it is as if the mother of towns has a tenderness that embraces the small towns around her.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{And whatever you have been given of a thing, it is the enjoyment of the life of this world and its adornment. But what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Will you not then use your reason?} (28:60)

The meaning of "of a thing" [min shay'], "whatever you have been given of a thing": of any thing from the necessities of life and from its refinements. "Then it is the enjoyment of the life of this world and its adornment": however exalted it may be, it is an enjoyment whose lifespan is short, as He, glorified is He, said: {Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little."} (4:77)

Therefore We have asked you not to become preoccupied with this enjoyment, and not to make it your goal, because your remaining in it is uncertain, and your enjoyment in it is according to the measure of your energy and movement.

We have already said that the blight of bliss in this world is that either it leaves you or you leave it, and that your lifetime in this world is not the lifetime of the world itself; rather, it is only the period of your own remaining in it. However much you attain of the world, death is inevitable.

Therefore our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, points us to another life that is lasting and certain, whose bliss does not depart from it and it does not depart from its bliss.

{And what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Will you not then use your reason?} (28:60)

"Better" [khayr]: because the bliss therein is not according to the measure of your energy, but according to the power of Allah, His bestowal and His generosity. "More lasting" [abqa]: because it is everlasting and does not cease. So if the sensible person compared the enjoyment of this world with the enjoyment of the Hereafter, he would choose the Hereafter.

Therefore, the Companion to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke about the reward of the martyr, and who became certain that there was nothing between him and Paradise except being killed in the way of Allah, was holding some dates in his hand that he was eating. He threw them away, and he saw that the duration of his chewing them was long, because it would stand between him and this goal. He threw them away and hastened to jihad to attain martyrdom. Why? Because he made a comparison between the enjoyment of this world and the enjoyment of the Hereafter.

And the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, when He makes this comparison between the disbelievers and the believers, says: {Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best things?"} (9:52) — either that we are victorious over you and humiliate you and take your good things, or that we attain martyrdom and go to something better than what we left. {And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Himself or at our hands.} (9:52)

So: you await for us only good, and we await for you only evil.

In another place He, glorified is He, said: {But you prefer the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting.} (87:16–17) Therefore He concluded the verse here with His saying, exalted is He: {Will you not then use your reason?} (28:60), because if reason compared the world and the Hereafter, it must choose the Hereafter.

(1) On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: A man said to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud: "Tell me, if I am killed, where will I be?" He said: "In Paradise." So he threw the dates in his hand, then fought until he was killed. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4046), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1899), in the Book of Leadership (Kitab al-Imarah). Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "I have not found the name of the man. Ibn Bashkuwal claimed that he was Umayr ibn al-Hammam, and al-Khatib preceded him in that. But it is explicitly stated in the hadith of Anas (in Muslim) that this was on the day of Badr... What appears is that they are two separate incidents that happened to two men, and Allah knows best."

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

{Is one to whom We have made a good promise, and who will certainly meet it, like one We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life and who, on the Day of Resurrection, will be among those brought forth (for punishment)? (28:61)}

This verse explains and emphasizes what came before it. A promise (wa'd) is good news of something good. When someone who is equal to you gives you good news of something good, its benefit comes in proportion to what he is able to do, and circumstances may sometimes prevent him from fulfilling his promise. But if the promise comes from God, its fulfillment comes in proportion to God's capacity to give, may He be exalted, and His promise never fails: ﴿And who is truer to his covenant than Allah?﴾ (9:111).

Therefore He said ﴿a good promise, and who will certainly meet it﴾ (28:61), meaning: definitely. ﴿Like one We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ (28:61), which is certainly transient. ﴿And who, on the Day of Resurrection, will be among those brought forth﴾ (28:61), meaning: for punishment.

This word ﴿al-muhdarin﴾ (28:61), "those brought forth," is not used in the Qur'an except for punishment, and perhaps the one who coined the word (muhdar) intended this meaning, because a muhdar never brings good.

He, the Exalted, says elsewhere: ﴿And they [the jinn] certainly know that they will be brought forth [for punishment]﴾ (37:158), and He said: ﴿And if it were not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth﴾ (37:57).

Footnote 1, occasion of revelation: On the authority of Mujahid, he said: It was revealed concerning Ali, Hamza, and Abu Jahl. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning Ammar and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. It was also said: It was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Jahl. [Cited by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 194.] Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5190): "Al-Qushayri said: The correct view is that it was revealed concerning the believer and the disbeliever in general. Al-Tha'labi said: In sum, it was revealed concerning every disbeliever who was given enjoyment in this world through well-being and wealth while in the Hereafter he has the Fire, and concerning every believer who was patient under the trials of this world, trusting in Allah's promise, and in the Hereafter has Paradise."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 28, verse 62:

Then He, glorified be He, says, emphasizing this summoning on the Day of Resurrection so that the disbeliever does not think he can escape: ﴿And the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾

The question here is addressed to those who associated partners (with God), not to those with whom they associated. The word ﴿Day﴾ (yawm) in this verse is in the accusative of time (zarf), so we must supply a verb that fits it. The estimate (taqdir) is: "And mention the Day He calls to them." The command is addressed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), but whom does the Messenger of God mention it to? He mentions it to the disbelievers, concerning this Day, the Day of Resurrection.

The verse gives us a snapshot of this Day, which is the Day of the Inevitable Event (al-Waqi'a), with no event after it; the Day of the Reality (al-Haqqa), that is, the Certain Truth that cannot be shifted from; the Day of the Shriek (al-Sakha), that is, the one that deafens the ears that turned away from it in the world; the Day of the Overwhelming Calamity (al-Tamma), which overwhelms; and the Day of Recompense (al-Din), that is, the Day on which religion (or recompense) benefits.

The Truth, glorified be He, mentions this snapshot for two matters:

The first: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was opposed, harmed, mocked, and ridiculed, and all means of punishment were gathered against him by his adversaries; they plotted against him by deceit and crafted magic for him, and so on.

Whenever you find a call met with this fierceness, know that it was met with this opposition only because it will demolish a corruption from which a people benefit, a people whom the word of reform terrifies, because it strikes them in their interests, their desires, their status, their arrogance, and their tyranny. It is natural that they stand against it.

Therefore we find many Westerners recognizing the greatness of Islam from the fierceness of its opponents' enmity. They say: "If this religion were not against their corruption, they would not have conspired against it; and if it were a trivial matter, they would have left it to time to erase it. But they were certain that it is the truth that will take away their falsehood and put an end to their tyranny."

So the Truth, glorified be He, commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to mention that Day: he mentions it to himself, and he mentions it to his people so that they may take heed. Perhaps when they hear what this Day contains of severity, disgrace, and punishment, they will reconsider themselves and repent to God.

Thus, God the Exalted's purpose in this action is not to terrify them but to warn them, lest disbelief befall them that brings them to this standing, just as you make your son aware of the consequences of negligence and warn him of failing so that he shuns its causes and seeks the causes of success.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the Day He calls to them﴾. He had called them in the world: "O people," "O children of Adam," so they plugged their ears and turned away from the call of God. Today He calls them with a call they cannot stop their ears against, because ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer﴾ (Qur'an 40:16). It is as though the Truth reminds them of this Day, perhaps they will heed and perhaps they will return.

The second matter: the verse came as consolation for our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). His Lord says to him: Do not despair at what they do to you, and do not let their scheming and obstinacy grieve you, for I will deal with them in such and such a way. You can perceive the secret of this psychological reassurance in the soul of the oppressed and the wronged when his child complains to him that his brother struck or humiliated him, and you say to please him: "Wait, I will do such and such to him." You see the child dazzled by this announced punishment and made happy by it, and likewise when the Messenger of God hears the punishment that will befall his enemies for what they did, he is gladdened by it and his soul is consoled for what he encounters.

The content of the call is: ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾ He did not say "My partners" and stop; rather He described them as ﴿whom you used to claim﴾ because He, glorified be He, is One with no partner, and these are partners only in their claim. And claim, as they say, is the mount of falsehood. Therefore they will find no answer to this question: ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾

Had they had partners before them, they would have said: "Here they are, those who misled us, so give them, O Lord, a double punishment." But they did not answer, and this is evidence that they do not exist. These polytheists stood bewildered, not knowing an answer, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Then the news will be obscured to them﴾ (Qur'an 28:66).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

{They will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones whom we misled; we misled them just as we ourselves went astray. We disassociate ourselves before You; it was not us that they worshipped."} (28:63)

The speech here is addressed to the associates who led the polytheists astray and misguided them. The meaning of ﴿حق عليهم﴾ (haqqa 'alayhim, "the word has become due against them") is: it was established and took effect; it is a matter that cannot be avoided, and there is no longer any room to turn it away from them, as He, glorified is He, says elsewhere: ﴿So the word of our Lord has become due against us; indeed, we will taste [the punishment]﴾ (37:31).

And Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And the word has come into effect against them because of what they did wrong, so they cannot speak﴾ (27:85)

But what is the word that took effect, became established for them, and became due against them? The word is: each one of you has a place with Me in Paradise on the assumption that you all believed, and each one of you has a place in the Fire on the assumption that you all disbelieved.

And what did they say? They said: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones whom we misled; we misled them just as we ourselves went astray...﴾ (28:63). Glory be to Allah! Now you say "Our Lord" and acknowledge His lordship, just as He, the Exalted, said regarding Pharaoh: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters?﴾ (10:91).

Now you acknowledge, after choice has been taken from you, and you no longer have any will even over your limbs and parts: your hand with which you used to strike, your foot with which you used to walk, and your tongue... all of them have left your will and are no longer under your command, because they are now subject to the command of Allah: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ (24:24).

The meaning of ﴿These are the ones whom we misled...﴾ (28:63) is: the polytheists. ﴿We misled them just as we ourselves went astray...﴾ (28:63) means: so that we may be equal. This is the reason for their misguidance: that they should be equal in loss. Otherwise, the people of falsehood strive hard to bring down the people of truth so that they may share their falsehood with them and be like them.

This matter gives us the psychological impulse of every deviant person when he sees a committed, upright one who does not share his corruption and deviation; it grieves him to be in the abyss alone, and why should others be distinguished from him? Read His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be equal﴾ (4:89).

Do you not see the people of falsehood, corruption, and immorality mocking the people of truth and ridiculing them, to make them averse to goodness and righteousness, and to deceive them with what they are in, until a person committed to his religion and the law of his Lord is not spared from their tongues? As the Exalted says:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another﴾ (83:29-30).

And would that the matter ended at winking and insinuation! Rather, these people persist, and make their mockery of the people of faith and obedience a subject of amusement and entertainment: ﴿And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting﴾ (83:31). That is: rejoicing and pleased with what they gained from the people of obedience, which indicates that all of them are delighted by this matter and it satisfies something in their sick, spiteful souls.

But the believer, by nature, loves to be honored and to keep himself away from imitating these people. Therefore his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, takes up his defense, saying to him: Do not grieve, for We will avenge you, and We will mock them, and make them a laughingstock on a lasting day in which their punishment will never end:

﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, [reclining] on couches, looking [on]. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ (83:34-36).

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is pleasing His believing servants: "Does what they have come to please you? Have We been able to recompense them for what they committed against you?" "Yes, O Lord!" The mockery of the disbelievers toward the people of faith in the abode of transient falsehood has turned into mockery of them in the abode of lasting truth, and it is a constant mockery with no end.

Therefore: ﴿We misled them just as we ourselves went astray...﴾ (28:63), meaning: so that we may be equal, none of us better than the other. From this same premise Iblis misled Adam, because when he became arrogant and was expelled from the mercy of Allah, and from the status he enjoyed with the angels, he wanted to take Adam and his descendants along to this same destination; it was painful to his soul to face this destiny alone, while Adam and his descendants enjoyed the mercy and pleasure of Allah.

For this reason we find Iblis, may Allah curse him, not content that his offspring should mislead the descendants of Adam; rather, he asks Allah to reprieve him until the Day of Resurrection so that he himself may directly undertake this misguidance. He is the great "teacher," and it is as if he fears that the capacities of his offspring for misguidance may not satisfy him; so he takes this task upon himself, saying: ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾ (7:16).

Some understand His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "Reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected." He said, "Indeed, you are among those reprieved"﴾ (7:14-15), as meaning that Allah answered Iblis's request. But ﴿Indeed, you are among those reprieved﴾ (7:15) is not an answer; rather, it is an affirmation of something that already existed before he asked. The meaning is that your request has no meaning, for you are already among the reprieved. Why? They say: because Allah wants Iblis, who misled Adam and expelled him from Paradise, to remain before his descendants, so that he may always remind them: "This is the one who misled your father Adam."

As for their saying: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones whom we misled; we misled them just as we ourselves went astray...﴾ (28:63), we pause at ﴿these﴾ (hā'ulā'), which is a demonstrative for the plural of both kinds. You say: hā'ulā' al-rijāl (these men) and hā'ulā' al-nisā' (these women). It consists of: the hā' is for alerting, and ulā' is a demonstrative; likewise in hādhā, hādhihi, hādhān, hātān. The hā' serves to alert the listener that you are about to speak, so that he gives you his attention and is attentive to what you say, so that nothing of your speech escapes him.

This is when you address someone like yourself, since he needs alerting. But when you address your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, it is bad manners to use an alerting particle in addressing Him, as the polytheists did. Since they said ﴿Our Lord...﴾ (28:63), it is not proper for them to say ﴿these...﴾ (28:63). Would they alert Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?

Therefore we observe this courtesy in the address of the Prophet of Allah, Musa, peace be upon him, as the Qur'an relates of him: ﴿"And what hastened you from your people, O Musa?" He said, "They are right behind me on my path, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased"﴾ (20:83-84). He said "ulā'" (they) without the alerting hā', out of courtesy toward his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

We also observe that you find no address from the disbelievers except with hā'ulā': ﴿Our Lord, these have misled us...﴾ (7:38), ﴿Our Lord, these are our associates...﴾ (16:86). As for the believer, it is never fitting for him to alert Allah, the Exalted; nor should such a thing proceed from one believer to another, because he is always attentive.

Then they say: ﴿We disassociate ourselves before You; it was not us that they worshipped﴾ (28:63). Now they reverse course, as they said before: ﴿Our Lord...﴾ (28:63). Now they say: ﴿We disassociate ourselves before You...﴾ (28:63). But this disavowal will not benefit them; their time has ended, and the period of obligation and choice has passed. Now is the time of reckoning and the removal of will and choice. How much they resemble Pharaoh when Allah said to him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ (10:91).

As for their saying: ﴿It was not us that they worshipped﴾ (28:63), the associates say: we had no coercive power by which we compelled you to worship us, nor any power of authority or argument by which we persuaded you; rather, you were waiting for a signal from us, as their chief Iblis said: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves...﴾ (14:22).

Therefore, these polytheists were in fact worshipping themselves and their own selves, since the associates were idols or other things, having no method to speak by and to call people to worship them. Otherwise, what did the idols, the sun, or the stars say to those who worshipped them? What did they command them, and what did they forbid them?

Therefore, it is a god without a method and without obligations, and this is what the polytheists desire, because what troubles people in the matter of belief in divinity is what it entails of obligations, and what it imposes of command or prohibition that stands between the human soul and what it desires, and halts it at limits it may not exceed.

Therefore: ﴿It was not us that they worshipped﴾ (28:63); rather, they worship themselves, and worship their desires and appetites. How easy it is for a person to worship gods that obligate him to nothing, so he walks through life according to his whim; this is what promoted the worship of these gods.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, wants to establish against man the proof that his own self is the first means to his desires. Otherwise, if the whole matter were merely the whispering of Satan, then who misled Iblis into disobedience first? As the poet said:

*Iblis, when he disobeyed, who was it that whispered to him?*

Therefore, it is the pride of the self and its appetites, and Satan has nothing but to show it, and it falls. For this reason the noble Hadith says: "When Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, and the devils are chained."

Since the devils are chained, they have no movement among mankind; for Allah knows that we attribute all our sins to Satan. It is as if He, glorified is He, says: Behold, the devils have been shackled and chained; so who misled you and adorned for you while they are chained? Therefore it is your own self that whispers to you. That is why we say: every sin that occurs in Ramadan has no share of Satan in it; it is only the appetite of the self.

We have previously explained how to distinguish between a sin that comes from Satan and one that is an appetite of the self. If the sin keeps you fixed upon it, not shifting from it to something else, then it is from Satan, because he, God forbid, wants you to be disobedient in any way and by any means, and so he moves you to another sin in which he can get you to fall. Unlike the appetite of the self, which wants a particular thing for its own sake and wants nothing else.

1 *Anzirhu*: delay him, give him respite, and be patient with him. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "Reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected"﴾ (7:14), means: give me respite and postpone my reckoning and punishment until the Day of Resurrection. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/273].

2 Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/281) and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (4/128), from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "When Ramadan comes, the gates of Mercy are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained."

Then the Truthful Lord says:

{And it will be said, "Call upon your partners," so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided!}

He had earlier called out to them, ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾ [al-Qasas 28:62], meaning: according to your claim, because He, glory be to Him, has no partners. Here He says to them, ﴿Call upon your partners, so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment; if only they had been guided!﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64]. He did not say "My partners," even though they had taken them as partners to Allah.

So what is the meaning of ﴿your partners﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64]? Is it in the claim of divinity? No, because they are followers of them. So what then is the meaning of ﴿your partners﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64]? The scholars said: the idafah (annexation, possessive construction) comes with three meanings. It may mean "min" (from), as in: ardabb qamh (an ardab of wheat), meaning "of wheat." Or it may mean "fi" (in), as in: makr al-layl (the plotting of the night), meaning "plotting in the night." Or it may mean the lam of ownership, as in: qalam Zayd (Zayd's pen), meaning "a pen for Zayd."

So the meaning here of ﴿your partners﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64] is: from your kind, or among you, meaning they are not distinguished from you in anything. And the deity must be of a higher kind; if he is of your kind, then he is equal to you, and is not fit for you to take as a god.

The meaning of ﴿Call upon your partners﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64] is: call them so that they will help you and intercede for you, as you said: ﴿These are our intercessors with Allah﴾ [Yunus 10:18], and as you said: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ [al-Zumar 39:3].

So: call upon them so that they will bring you near to Allah and intercede for you. The one who performs this task must have a station with Allah that guarantees it. Do these partners guarantee a station with Allah? How could they, when they cannot guarantee one for themselves?

﴿So they will call upon them﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64], "O our partners, O you whom we were told such-and-such about, help us!" ﴿But they will not respond to them﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64], because they are occupied with themselves. ﴿And they will see the punishment; if only they had been guided!﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64], meaning: if they had been guided by the guidance of Allah and the guidance of His Messenger, and had seen the punishment with which he warned them as a reality and a fact from which there is no escape, this would not have happened to them, and they would not have faced this outcome.

Or: when they saw the punishment as a reality in the Hereafter, they wished that they had been guided.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 28, verse 65:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

{And on the Day He calls to them and says, "What answer did you give to the messengers?" (65) Then the information will be obscured to them that Day, and they will not question one another. (66)}

He says here too, ﴿He calls to them...﴾ [al-Qasas 65]. So what is the purpose of all these calls? They are for rebuke, for reproach, and for mockery of them, and of those who worshipped them and followed them besides Allah. The content of the call is ﴿What answer did you give to the messengers?﴾ [al-Qasas 65]. The answer (ijabah) is the agreement of the one who is asked with what is demanded of him. So what was your answer to them after you had believed in a God? Did you act upon the rulings they brought? Did you have from them certain, true knowledge?

This question is for incapacitation (ta'jiz), because if they attempt to answer they will find no answer, and they will be shamed and embarrassed. For this reason He says after it, ﴿Then the information will be obscured to them...﴾ [al-Qasas 66], meaning: the proofs and excuses were hidden from them, and they were blind to them, so they did not see them. ﴿And they will not question one another.﴾ [al-Qasas 66] They possess nothing but silence, as they said: silence is the answer to what one dislikes. And as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And no close friend will ask a close friend* [al-Ma'arij 10]

These do not question one another because they are equal in ignorance and partners in misguidance, and each of them is preoccupied with himself: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother (34) and his mother and his father (35) and his companion and his children (36). For every man among them, on that Day, there will be a matter that occupies him.* [Abasa 34-37]

Just as the polytheists were asked, ﴿What answer did you give to the messengers?﴾ [al-Qasas 65], in another place the messengers are asked: ﴿On the Day Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What answer were you given?..."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 109], meaning: concerning what you knew of knowledge. Its first part is the supreme certain knowledge, and its second is the knowledge of the rulings. So what answer did the people give you?

Consider here the courtesy of the messengers and the extent of their understanding in the station of answering to God, while they know full well what their peoples answered, and that among them were those who believed in them and devoted themselves to serving their call and sacrificed and were martyred, and among them were those who disbelieved and obstinately opposed; yet they say: ﴿They say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [al-Ma'idah 109]

How can they say ﴿We have no knowledge...﴾ [al-Ma'idah 109] while they know? They said: because they were not certain whether one who believed did so from conviction or not. They take the outward appearances of people, while their inner states none knows but Allah. It is as if they are saying: You, our Lord, ask about the answer of truth, not the answer of hypocrisy, and the answer of truth we do not know; and You, glory be to You, are the Knower of the unseen.

So they made the Truth, blessed and exalted, the legislative authority, the judicial authority, and the executive authority in the court of divine justice, in which it will be proclaimed before all witnesses: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?...﴾ [Ghafir 16]

The question among the Arabs is used in two ways: either for knowledge, where you ask in order to know, as a student asks his teacher; or the question is for acknowledgment of what you already know, as a teacher asks his student so that he confesses against himself. Of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So on that Day no one will be asked about his sin, man or jinn* [al-Rahman 39], meaning a question of knowledge, because We know.

And His saying: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned* [al-Saffat 24], meaning a question of acknowledgment from them, even though My speech on the Day of Resurrection is a proof, because it cannot be turned back; but nonetheless We question them so that they may acknowledge, and bear witness against themselves.

The Truth, blessed and exalted, shows you that He, exalted is He, displays the scenes of the Day of Resurrection upon the disbelievers, not because He hates them, but He wants them to bring this dreadful image to mind, that perhaps they may refrain and repent; therefore He opens the door of repentance for them, for He is Lord and Merciful.

For this reason there came in the sacred hadith: "The earth said: O Lord, permit me to swallow up the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks. And the mountains said: O Lord, permit me to fall upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks. And the seas said: O Lord, permit me to drown the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks. Then He, exalted is He, said: Leave Me and My creation; if you had created them, you would have had mercy on them. Leave them, for if they repent to Me, I am their beloved, and if they do not repent, I am their physician."(1)

I treat them with encouragement once and with warning another time; I make them yearn for Paradise and fear the Fire; and I open the door of repentance. The opening of the door of repentance is not only a mercy from Allah to the penitent, but a mercy for everyone who suffers through the disobedience of one who does not repent.

If the door of repentance were closed in the face of the disobedient, he would despair and become a "lost one" (fa'id) by whom society suffers all his life. So the opening of the door of repentance is a mercy to the penitent, a mercy to his society, and indeed to all humanity: a mercy to the disobedient and to those who have been scorched by the fire of disobedience.

1. Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/281), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (4/128), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "When Ramadan enters, the gates of mercy are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained."
