Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 28, verse 66:

Repeated text, because it shares wording with verse 65: Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

{And the day He calls to them and says, "What did you answer the messengers?" (65). Then the news will be obscured from them that day, and they will not question one another (66).}

He says here also, ﴿And the day He calls to them...﴾ (28:65). So what is the purpose of all these calls? They are for reproach, rebuke, and mockery of them, and of those who worshipped them and followed them besides Allah. The content of the call is ﴿What did you answer the messengers?﴾ (28:65). The answer (ijabah) is the fulfilment of what the one asking requires. So what was your answer to them after you had believed in a God? Did you act upon the rulings they brought? Did you gain from them certain, true knowledge?

This question is asked to make them incapable (ta'jiz), for if they try to answer they will find no answer, and so they will be disgraced and ashamed. Therefore He says after it, ﴿Then the news will be obscured from them...﴾ (28:66), meaning: the proofs and excuses became hidden from them, and they became blind to them and did not see them. ﴿So they will not question one another﴾ (28:66), meaning they have no power except silence, as they say: silence is the answer to what one dislikes. And as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask after his intimate friend (10)﴾ (al-Ma'arij).

These people do not ask one another, because in ignorance they are equal, and in misguidance they are partners, and each of them is preoccupied with himself: ﴿The day a man flees from his brother (34), and his mother and his father (35), and his spouse and his children (36). For every man among them, that day, is a matter that occupies him (37)﴾ (Abasa).

Just as the polytheists were asked ﴿What did you answer the messengers?﴾ (28:65), in another place the messengers are asked: ﴿The day Allah gathers the messengers and says, "What was your answer..."﴾ (5:109), meaning: in what you knew of knowledge. Its first part is the highest certainty of knowledge, and its second part is knowledge of the rulings. So what did people answer you with?

Consider here the courtesy of the messengers and the extent of their understanding in the station of answering to God, while they know full well what their peoples answered, and that some of them believed in them and devoted themselves to serving their call, sacrificing and being martyred, and some disbelieved and was obstinate. Yet they say: ﴿They say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You, You are the Knower of the unseen" (5:109)﴾.

How then do they say ﴿We have no knowledge...﴾ (5:109) when they know? They said: because they were not certain whether those who believed did so from conviction or not. They take people by their outward appearance, while their inner states none knows but Allah. It is as if they are saying: You, our Lord, ask about the answer of truth, not the answer of hypocrisy, and the answer of truth we do not know; You, glory be to You, are the Knower of the unseen.

Thus they made the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, the legislative authority, the judicial authority, and the executive authority in the court of divine justice, in which it will be proclaimed before all the witnesses: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? (16)﴾ (Ghafir).

The question among the Arabs is used in two ways: either for knowledge, where you ask in order to know, as a student asks his teacher; or the question is for acknowledgement of what you know, as a teacher asks his student so that he confesses against himself. Among this is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿So that Day, none will be asked about his sin, neither man nor jinn (39)﴾ (al-Rahman), meaning a question of knowledge, because We know.

And His saying: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned (24)﴾ (al-Saffat), meaning a question of acknowledgement from them, and although My speech on the Day of Resurrection is a proof, since it cannot be repelled, nevertheless We ask them so that they may acknowledge, and bear witness against themselves.

The Truth, blessed and exalted be He, shows you that He, exalted be He, displays the aspects of the Day of Resurrection upon the disbelievers, not because He hates them, but He wants them to call to mind this dreadful picture, so that perhaps they will be awakened and repent; therefore He opens for them the door of repentance, for He is Lord and Merciful.

Therefore there came in the sacred hadith: "The earth said: O Lord, permit me to swallow the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your bounty and withheld Your thanks. And the mountains said: O Lord, permit me to fall upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your bounty and withheld Your thanks. And the seas said: O Lord, permit me to drown the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your bounty and withheld Your thanks. Then He, exalted be He, said: Leave Me and My creation; if you had created them you would have shown them mercy. Leave them: if they repent to Me, I am their beloved, and if they do not repent, I am their physician."(1)

I treat them with encouragement at one time and with warning at another; I make them yearn for Paradise and fear the Fire; and I open the door of repentance. Opening the door of repentance is not only a mercy from Allah to the penitent, but a mercy to everyone who suffers from the disobedience of one who does not repent.

If the door of repentance were closed in the face of the disobedient, he would despair and become a "lost one" whose existence burdens society throughout his life. Therefore, opening the door of repentance is mercy to the penitent, mercy to his society, and indeed mercy to all humanity: mercy to the disobedient and to those who have been burned by the fire of disobedience.

1 Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/281) and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (4/128), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "When Ramadan enters, the gates of mercy are opened, the gates of Hellfire are closed, and the devils are chained."

Why did He use here ("ʿasā", which denotes hope) after saying ﴿Whoever repents, believes, and does righteous deeds...﴾ [al-Qasas: 67], and not say "he will be among the successful," thereby decisively affirming their success?

They said: Because perhaps he repents, but ʿasā (it is hoped) that he will persist in his repentance so that he may continue in success. Or we may say that ʿasā from Allah indicates certainty (taḥqīq). We have already said that hopes (rajāʾāt) are of degrees: hope expressed by the speaker is stronger than hope expressed about someone absent, and if the hope is in Allah, it is the strongest of all hopes.

Therefore, He, glory be to Him, says in His address to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [al-Isra: 79]. So what hope is stronger than hope placed in Allah?

In sum: ʿasā is a hope when it comes from one who does not possess the power to bring about what is hoped for, and it is a certainty when it comes from one who possesses the power to bring about what is hoped for, and He is Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses. They have no choice. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.} (28:68)

We were expecting the context to inform us of the punishment that would befall the polytheists, but instead comes the verse ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses...﴾ [al-Qasas: 68], as if the Truth, glorified is He, were saying: "I am the One who knows where the benefit lies, and I know how to relieve you of their evil. So leave Me to create what I will and choose what I will, for I am the Lord who cares for the one being nurtured, bringing him through upbringing to the purpose intended for him."

The one being nurtured is of two kinds: either a believer or a disbeliever. The believer is bound to suffer because of the disbeliever's deeds, and this suffering will extend if the disbeliever remains in his disbelief. Therefore repentance was prescribed for him, and his return was accepted, and this is the first thing that relieves the believers.

The meaning of ﴿They have no choice...﴾ [al-Qasas: 68] is: you have no option, so leave Me to choose for you, and then carry out what I choose.

Or: this verse ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses...﴾ [al-Qasas: 68] was revealed in response to their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31], meaning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira or Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. So Allah replied to them: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees...﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32].

How, then, can they hope to choose the means of mercy themselves, when We are the One who distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, making this one rich and that one poor, this one strong and that one weak? In worldly matters I have full control over them, so do they want to control the matters of the Hereafter and direct the mercy of Allah according to their own choice?!

﴿They have no choice...﴾ [al-Qasas: 68] means: the choice in such matters.

It may also be that ﴿They have no choice...﴾ [al-Qasas: 68] means: the believers have no right to object to Allah's acceptance of the repentance of the polytheists who harmed them. They might say: "Why does He accept repentance from them, when they did such-and-such to us, and we had wished to see them writhing in punishment?"

But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, chooses what He wills and does what He desires. When He accepts the repentance of a polytheist, He does not show mercy to him alone, but He also shows mercy to you, by relieving you of his evil.

As for His saying ﴿Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Qasas: 68], it means: Allah is exalted and far removed above what they desire, namely that they would have the Truth, glorified is He, descend in accordance with the wishes of people of desires among mankind. Had the Truth, glorified is He, descended in accordance with the desires of people of desires among mankind, whose desires differ, their lives would all have been corrupted.

Do you not see that people all differ in their inclinations and desires, and even in all matters of life? You see a group of them of the same age and the same social standing, yet when they set out to buy a commodity, for example, each one chooses a type and a color different from the other's.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 28, verse 69:

What their breasts conceal, i.e., the secret (sirr): ﴿He knows the secret and what is yet more hidden﴾ [Ta-Ha]. The secret (sirr) is what you have kept locked within yourself and concealed from creation, which no one knows but you; or the secret is what you have confided to another, and at that moment it will no longer remain a secret. And if your breast is strained by your affair, the breast of another is more strained.

Since Allah, glorified is He, bestows favour upon us by making His knowledge encompass the secret, He knows the open (jahr) all the more, for it is something all people share and know. As for what is more hidden than the secret, it is because He, glorified is He, knows what you conceal in yourself before it exists in your breast; He alone knows things before they come into being.

You may ask: if one of His attributes, exalted is He, is that He knows the secret and what is more hidden than the secret, then what of the open, which is known to all? This question has perplexed some orientalists and their Muslim followers (the "dissolute" ones) who go along with them.

When we survey the verses of the Qur'an, we find that Allah, exalted is He, has made His knowledge equal between the secret and the open. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Whether of you conceals the speech or declares it aloud...﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 10].

He, glorified is He, also says: ﴿And keep your speech secret or declare it aloud...﴾ [al-Mulk: 13].

And the verse before us: ﴿Your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare﴾ [al-Qasas: 69]. In these verses the secret is placed before the open. But as for His saying, exalted is He:

﴿We shall make you recite, and you will not forget, except what Allah wills. Indeed He knows what is declared openly and what is hidden﴾ [al-A'la: 6–7].

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed He knows what is said openly and He knows what you conceal﴾ [al-Anbiya': 110]. Here He places the knowledge of the open before the knowledge of the secret, and the open is not placed first unless it has an aspect of concealment relative to the secret. This aspect was overlooked by the superficial thinkers, so they erred in understanding the verse.

For example, if you conceal something within yourself, it may appear in the slips of your tongue or in the features of your face, and perhaps your expression fails you and reveals what you concealed. Did not the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, say: ﴿And you will surely recognise them by the tone of their speech...﴾ [Muhammad: 30]?

So there are indications and signs by which we know the secret. As for the open, which is of the group, it is not a single openness, since it is set in contrast with the plural: ﴿Indeed He knows what is said openly and He knows what you conceal﴾ [al-Anbiya': 110]. The meaning is: and He knows what you declare openly and what you conceal.

Imagine yourself following a great crowd of people, each of whom chants a slogan. Can you distinguish these chants and trace each one back to its speaker? This is the riddle of the open and the aspect whose contemplation escaped them. Therefore Allah has favoured us with His knowledge of the open speech, which we do not know, however much we are equipped with instruments for separating and distinguishing sounds.

For this reason they say: you cannot pin down a crime within a crowd, because the voices and actions are mixed, each concealed within the other. As they say: the individual is protected by the group.

And they say: the masses are parrot-like, as Shawqi said in the defeat of Cleopatra, when they were routed on the day of (Actium) and spread the rumour that they had won. But this trick does not deceive the wise among the people, one of whom says to another about the mob-like nature of the masses:

Listen to the people, Dionysus, how they are inspired towards him
The air is filled with chanting: "by my life, those who slew him!"
Falsehood left its mark upon them, and the lie was imposed upon them.
What a parrot! Its mind is in its ears.

So the knowledge of the open here is a distinction deserving of Allah's favour, just as He favours us with the knowledge of the secret.

And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Your Lord knows...﴾ [al-Qasas: 69], to reassure the Messenger of Allah. For He is his Lord, the one who undertakes his upbringing and his care. He says to him: do not grieve over what they say, for I know their secret and their open speech. If you do not know what they say, I know it, and I will inform you of it. Did not He, glorified is He, say to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"...﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 8]?

So his Lord informed him of what passes even within souls, as if He, glorified is He, were saying to His Messenger: beware of thinking that I will call them to account only for what you know of their deeds, but for what you do not know of what they have done as well, so that the Messenger of Allah may be reassured that He, glorified is He, counts everything against them.

Then the Truthful One, glorified be He, says:

{He is Allah; there is no god but Him. To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.} (28:70)

Allah: He is the one truly worshipped, and to Him belong all attributes of perfection. And He, glorified be He, is "there is no god but Him..." (28:70). Since He alone is the One, no one can contest with Him or overrule Him in anything. He had already said to them: "Bring your partners" (28:62, 28:74) so that we may decide the matter of worship openly, and (nufasil) means: who holds this merchandise, that is, on the Day of Resurrection.

The meaning of "the first..." (28:70) is: the creation that Allah created, and the universe that He prepared to receive His vicegerent on earth: the sun, the moon, the stars, the trees, the mountains, the water, the air, and the earth. Before man came, Allah had prepared the universe to receive him.

Therefore, when the Truthful One speaks about Adam, He does not say that he was the first of creation; rather, he was the first of the children of Adam, for many worlds preceded him in creation. This is why He, exalted is He, says: "Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worthy of mention?" (76:1), meaning: he had no existence.

The preparation of the universe to receive man is a beautiful act that calls for praise and thanksgiving. Allah created for you the whole universe, then made you benefit from it, although you have no power over it or access to it. The sun serves you, while you cannot control it or own it, and it works for you without any maintenance from you, and without your needing a spare part. Likewise, the whole universe moves in your service and the fulfilment of your interests, and all of this deserves praise.

After Allah created you in a universe prepared for your service, He left you to roam in it: a seed in your father's back, a drop in your mother's womb, until you emerge into existence and her lap embraces you. He does not burden you except to reach the age of manhood and the years of maturity. He granted you reason and maturity so that you become capable of begetting one like yourself. This is the final sign of maturity in your formation, like the fruit, which does not come forth in its like until it has ripened and become complete.

Therefore we find that it is of Allah's wisdom that He does not give the fruit its sweetness except after its seed has ripened, so that when you plant it after eating, it sprouts like itself; had you eaten it before its ripening, its seed would not have produced anything, and this kind would have become extinct. Hence you see that when the ripe fruit is not picked, it falls to the ground for you, as if saying to you: "I am ready."

Thus in the countryside we observe, for example, the mulberry tree or the apricot tree: the ripe fruit falls to the ground and then sprouts a new plant that preserves the species; had the fruits fallen unripe, they would not have sprouted.

Likewise, man does not beget his like except after he has matured, and then Allah imposes obligations upon him, questions him and holds him to account. So man should recall Allah's favour upon him even before He summoned him into existence, and be certain that the One who now obligates him, commands him and forbids him is his Lord, his Creator and his Nurturer, who will impose on him only what is good for him. Therefore he must listen and obey.

As for His saying, "and in the last..." (28:70), it means: to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter, as He, glorified be He, said: "Their final call will be: Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds" (10:10). So one praises Allah in the Hereafter, because He gave me enjoyment in this world for a term, and gave me enjoyment in this world according to my capacity; whereas in the Hereafter He gives me without term, and according to His own capacity, glorified be He. When we see this bliss, we cannot but say: "Praise be to Allah." Thus praise belongs to Allah in both the first and the last.

As for His saying, "and to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned" (28:70), it is because the Hereafter exists only for judgment and for deciding disputes, where each person knows what is his and what is against him. So do not think that those who harmed you and wronged you will escape from our grip.

"And to Him you will be returned" (28:70) means: for reckoning. In one reading, "turja'un" (you are returned) is read in the active sense, because they will return to Us and come to Us of their own accord, as if they were set to it like an alarm clock set to a time; so when their appointed time comes, they come to Us on their own, without anyone driving them.

According to the reading "turja'un" (you are returned) [passive], beware lest you think you can refuse Us, as you refused Our messengers in this world; for the caller in this world would lead you with gentleness and kindness, but the caller of the Hereafter will gather you by force and against your will, and you will be unable to escape from it: "The Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent push" (52:13).

1 Yudda'un (they are pushed): that is, they will be driven with a violent push, by compulsion and harshness. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/228].

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

"Say: 'Have you considered? If Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen?' Say: 'Have you considered? If Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?'" (28:71-72)

Exalted be He, enumerates His blessings upon His servants in two matters that relate to the movement and rest of life. Movement brings good to people, and rest brings relief to one who is tired from movement. By his nature, a human being cannot give and labour except after rest. Whoever defies this nature, staying awake through the night and working by day, must eventually be exhausted, his strength depleted, and he cannot continue.

Therefore He, exalted be He, says: "By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears, and by Him who created the male and the female, indeed your endeavours are diverse." (92:1-4)

Each of the night and the day has its function, and likewise the man and the woman. So beware lest you confuse these functions, for otherwise life will be corrupted and its events will exhaust you. Before electricity and the entry of television and video into homes, our daily life would begin with activity at the dawn prayer, because we used to sleep after the night prayer. But now the situation is as you see. We used to greet our day with sound, vigorous movement, because we received the night with sound stillness and complete calm.

In the midst of enumerating His blessings upon us, the Truthful, glory be to Him, says: "Have you considered..." (28:71), meaning: tell me what you do. "...if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection..." (28:71), meaning: throughout your lives. "...what god other than Allah could bring you light?" (28:71). Sarmad (perpetual) means that which is lasting and continuous.

He said "light" (diya') and did not say "nur" (noor), because nur may come from the stars and may come from the moon, whereas diya', which is light, rays and heat, comes only from the sun.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: "It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light..." (10:5)

And He said: "what god other than Allah could bring you light?" (28:71), and did not say "who could bring you light", in order to draw our attention to the fact that this matter is beyond the power of anyone but a god, and there is no god but Allah. In light you see things, and you walk on guidance, so you carry out the movements of your life without collision or disorder. By light I coexist with things in safety for myself and for them. Otherwise, if we walked in darkness, we would shatter or shatter what is around us, for when you walk in darkness you either break what is weaker than you, or what is stronger than you breaks you.

Just as light exists in material things, it likewise has a role in immaterial things. The light of immaterial things is the values that govern the movement of life and balance it, and protect you from breaking the weaker than you, or from the stronger breaking you. Therefore it was logical that He, exalted be He, should say: "It is He who blesses you, and His angels, that He may bring you out of darknesses into light..." (33:43)

The intended meaning is: from the darknesses of meanings into the light of values, not the darknesses of matter, for I cannot dispense with it for my comfort, and it has a role for me no less than the role of light. Therefore, in describing His light, He, mighty and majestic, says: "Light upon light..." (24:35)

A material light by which you see the things around you, so that you do not stumble among them, and your movement is preserved. This material light is shared by believer and disbeliever, and benefits both the obedient and the disobedient; He has not withheld it from anyone of His creation. As for immaterial light, the light of guidance, the light of certainty and of values, this He sends through the hands of His messengers. When the believer takes both lights, he benefits from them in this world, and their benefit extends to him until the Day of Resurrection. Therefore after it He said:

"Allah guides to His light whom He wills, and Allah sets forth parables for people..." (24:35)

Since the noble verse began with "Say", it is fitting to close it with His saying: "Will you not then listen?" (28:71), meaning: listen to what I tell you and reflect upon it.

1 Al-sarmad: the permanence of time, whether night or day. A long night is "sarmad." Al-Zajjaj said: al-sarmad is what is lasting in the language. And al-sarmad: that which is perpetual and does not cease. [Lisan al-Arab – root: s-r-m-d]

Then Allah bestows favor by mentioning the verse that corresponds to the night, namely the verse of the day: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?﴾ That is, perpetual, having no end.

You notice that these two verses follow one pattern, but their concluding phrases differ, which shows the eloquence and inimitability of the Qur'an: every meaning is matched with what suits it. In the verse of the night He said ﴿Will you not then hear?﴾, and in the verse of the day He said ﴿Will you not then see?﴾. This is because the eye has no function at night; rather, the ear does. You hear without seeing, and it is through hearing that summoning takes place.

As for the day, and with the presence of light, the function belongs to the eye, by which one sees. So this is a wise closing for the verses, placing each meaning where it fits.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 28, verse 73:

Then Allah, exalted is He, summarizes these two verses in His saying, glorified is He:

{And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.} (28:73)

After Allah had explained the matter of the night and the day separately, each on its own, He combined them, because they are together a manifestation of the manifestations of Allah's mercy. In the verse there is a rhetorical feature that they call (al-laff wa al-nashr) (the "wrapping and unfolding" device, in which several items are mentioned together and then each is matched with its corresponding element). After Allah combined the night and the day, He informed about them with His saying: {that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty} (28:73), trusting in the discernment of the listener, and that he would return each of them to what fits it. So the night corresponds to {that you may rest therein} (28:73), and the day corresponds to {and that you may seek of His bounty} (28:73).

Al-laff, that is, the gathering of the things judged together in one part, and the judgment in another part; and al-nashr is returning each judgment to its owner.

We give as an example of this the verse of al-Taymuriyya:
My heart, my eyelid, and the tongue, and the sword (are) a striver, a weeper, a grateful one, and a forgiving one.
Here you have gathered the things judged in the first half-line and the judgments in the second half-line, and you must return each judgment to its owner.

The night and the day are two complementary signs, and by them the movement of life is ordered; for if you do not rest, you cannot be capable of work, because you have energy, and in your body are generators of energy. So at the moment you tire, you find that your limbs have slackened and been exhausted, and this is a warning to you; your members alert you that you are no longer fit for movement, and you must have rest in order to regain your activity anew.

Rest is in proportion to fatigue. Perhaps you rest when you stand, for example, while walking; if standing does not give you rest, you sit or lie down; if fatigue increases, sleep overcomes you, and it is the self-restraint that checks its possessor if he rebels against the nature which Allah created in him.

And it is strange that some people go out of this nature: they take stimulants so that sleep does not overcome them, and they take sedatives in order to sleep. Had they surrendered themselves to its nature, sleeping when sleep comes upon them and working when they find in themselves the energy for work, they would have relieved themselves of many hardships.

Therefore they say: sleep is a guest; if you welcome it, it refreshes you, and if you seek it, it wearies you. And until now, despite the progress of the sciences, they have not reached the secret of sleep, and how a person enters it quietly and gently without being aware of its reality. I challenge any of us to know how he sleeps.

Therefore Allah made sleep one of His signs, exalted is He, like the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and He said, glorified is He: {And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day} (30:23).

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

{And on the Day He will call out to them, saying: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"}

The calling out had already occurred twice before, yet there is no repetition of this meaning, because each call has its own specific purpose. The call in the first instance is directed at those whom they associated with God, and concerns what they said before God, may He be exalted: ﴿"Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray; we led them astray just as we went astray..."﴾ [al-Qasas: 63]

As for the second, the call is directed to the polytheists: ﴿"What answer did you give to the messengers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 65]

As for here, the call concerns the matter of bearing witness against them. Therefore, the phrase "where" (ayna), "My partners" (shuraka'i), and "whom you used to claim" (alladhina kuntum tazʿumun) form a common element across the three verses, but what is required in each differs from what is required in the other. So there is no repetition in the matter; rather, it is emphasis in the whole.

(1) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5196): "The calling out here is not from God, because God, exalted is He, does not speak to the disbeliever, due to His saying: ﴿And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 174]. Rather, He commands whoever will rebuke and reproach them, and establish the proof against them at the station of reckoning. It was also said: it is possible that it is from God, and His saying ﴿And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 174] refers to when it is said to them: ﴿Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108]."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 28, verse 75:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

{And We will draw forth from every nation a witness, and We will say: "Bring your proof." Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them.}

That is: We will bring out from every nation its prophet and present him, so that he may be a witness against it. ﴿Then We will say: "Bring your proof."﴾ [al-Qasas 75] "Show us your partners whom you took besides Allah. Where are they, that they may defend you?" But far from it: they have strayed from them and fled from them.

﴿So the news will be obscured from them that Day, and they will not question one another.﴾ [al-Qasas 66]

So: your partners have vanished, and your witnesses have vanished, but Our witnesses are present. ﴿And We will draw forth from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas 75], who testifies that the method of Allah was conveyed to them. If you say: "Indeed, Satan misled us, and the misguiders among mankind misled us," We will reply that We did not leave you to be led astray by them, so that you would have an excuse. Rather, We sent Messengers to you to guide you, and the Messengers have conveyed to you.

In another place, He, exalted is He, says: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these people?﴾ [al-Nisa' 41]

So what will be their state on the Day when you bear witness against them that you conveyed the message and were thorough in the conveyance, and that you were persecuted by them and harmed, while their partners have strayed from them and they find no one to testify for them or defend them? Then their excuses fall away, and the tribunal will have become clear (tanawwarat).

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿"Bring your proof."﴾ [al-Qasas 75] That is: say, "Our Messengers did not convey Our method to you," and bring forward an argument that will repel [punishment] from you. When they become bewildered and remorse falls upon them, since their witnesses have disappeared and the witnesses against them have appeared, ﴿then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas 75].

They will be taken by surprise, as He, exalted is He, says of them: ﴿And Allah found him there and paid him his account in full﴾ [al-Nur 39], and He says: ﴿And they will find what they did present there﴾ [al-Kahf 49].

They will be surprised by what they did not believe in and did not affirm. But what is the reason for this surprise, when We had informed them of it in the world and given them a warning which they should have heeded, and should have prepared themselves for this standing? The intelligent person, when you warn him of the roughness of the road he will travel and of its dangers and terrors, ought to turn away from it, if the one advising him is sincere. And he has nothing to lose, when he takes precaution for himself, if his adviser turns out to be lying, in accordance with the saying of the poet:

"The astrologer and the physician both claim
that bodies will not be resurrected. I say to you both:
if your saying is true, I have not lost,
and if it is true, the loss is yours."

And what harm is there for you, if you carry a rifle on this frightening road and then find nothing to frighten you? So: if you do not lose, you will gain nothing; and if we do not gain, we will lose nothing.

His saying ﴿and what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them﴾ [al-Qasas 75] means: it disappeared, namely the claim of partners.

After the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has given us a snapshot of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, and the Resurrection frightens only those who believe in it. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter and the Resurrection, there must be another deterrent for them, because the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to protect the soundness of the universe and the movement of life.

Had the requital been limited to the Resurrection, the non-believers would have run riot and their corruption would have spread, and people would have suffered because of them. Allah, exalted is He, wants to protect the movement of life from the corrupters among the non-believers in the Hereafter, so He makes for them a punishment in this world before the punishment of the Hereafter.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And indeed for those who have done wrong there is a punishment short of that﴾ [al-Tur 47].

That is: before the punishment of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 28, verse 76:

The punishment that befalls the disbelievers in this world is a deterrent for every oppressor who tries to transgress and to stand in the way of the truth. Therefore our Lord, glorified is He, gives us a picture of this worldly punishment for those who spread corruption in the earth, and so He, glorified is He, says:

{Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he oppressed them. And We had given him of treasures whose keys would be a burden to a band of strong men. When his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant."}

He does not speak here of Qarun's recompense in the Hereafter; rather, He makes him an example and a clear lesson in this world for everyone who does not believe in the Day of Resurrection, so that he may be deterred.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was persecuted by the disbelievers of Quraysh, who stood against his call, harmed his companions, until they became unable to protect themselves. Nevertheless, the Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and will turn their backs⦁ [al-Qamar, 45]

Then 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was astonished: "What multitude is this? We are unable to protect ourselves!" But when Badr took place, the disbelievers were defeated and killed. 'Umar said: "Yes, Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and will turn their backs⦁ [al-Qamar, 45]

Therefore they say: No oppressor dies in this world until Allah takes vengeance upon him, and the oppressed sees in him a day that cools his burning rage. When an oppressor died in Syria and the people did not see in him any sign of Allah's vengeance, they were astonished, and one of them said: "Surely Allah has taken vengeance upon him without our noticing. If he escaped the punishment of this world, then beyond this abode there is another abode in which the doer of good is recompensed for his good and the doer of evil for his evil, and the justice of Allah, glorified is He, requires this accounting."

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, makes Qarun a lesson for everyone who does not believe in the Hereafter, so that he may fear the punishment of Allah and beware of His retribution. And where is the lesson here? In Qarun, the head of the people, the richest of their rich, and the chief of their strongmen. When Allah seizes such a man, his seizure is a lesson for those below him.

We were told that a friend of ours worked at the customs house of Alexandria, and some of his colleagues, strongmen who wanted to impose their control over others, gathered against him. He took their leader, threw him to the ground, and then the others dispersed and left him alone.

From this same principle Allah, exalted is He, seized Qarun, who was a strongman and a symbol of wealth and dignity among his people. So He said, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses... 76﴾ [al-Qasas] So, when we contemplate the life of Moses, peace be upon him, we find that he was afflicted with the chiefs of disbelief: he confronted Pharaoh, who claimed divinity, and he confronted Haman, and then the Samiri, who betrayed him among his people in his absence and called them to worship the calf.

And he was afflicted from his own people by Qarun. As for the meaning of "from his people": either because he was of his kin among the Children of Israel, or "his people" means those who lived with him. The Qur'an does not go into this matter beyond this, but the exegetes say that he was Moses' cousin: Qarun son of Yashhar son of Qahath son of Lawi son of Ya'qub, while Moses is the son of 'Imran son of Qahath son of Lawi son of Ya'qub.

The historians have spoken about the enmity between Moses and Qarun. They said: When Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord to strengthen his arm with his brother Harun, He answered him: ﴿He said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses."⦁ [Ta-Ha, 36] And this was not the first time, but ﴿We had already bestowed favor upon you another time⦁ [Ta-Ha, 37] And Allah sent with him his brother Harun, because he was more eloquent in speech than Moses, and He made them partners in the message and addressed them both together: ﴿Go, you and your brother⦁ [Ta-Ha, 43] to affirm that the message did not originate from within Moses.

If you see the address in the Qur'an directed to Moses alone, know that Harun is implicitly included in it. Among this is when Moses prayed against the people of Pharaoh, saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, so that they may lead astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment⦁ [Yunus, 88]

The one who made the supplication was Moses, yet when his Lord answered him, He said: ﴿Your supplication has been answered, so remain on the right course⦁ [Yunus, 89] This is evidence that Harun was not a messenger from within Moses, but from Allah, glorified is He; and also evidence that the one who affirms a supplication is like the one who supplicates: Moses would supplicate while Harun said, "Amin."

When Moses went to the appointed time with his Lord, he said to his brother: ﴿Take my place among my people⦁ [al-A'raf, 142] During Moses' absence the affair of the calf occurred, and Moses became angry with his brother Harun. When matters calmed between them, a distinction was made in the mission of each of them: Harun was given the (ḥubura), and the ḥibr is the scholar who is regarded as a reference, just as he was given the (qurban), that is, drawing near to Allah.

At that, Qarun became angry, because he came out of this matter empty-handed, while his paternal cousins were distinguished by the message and the rank, despite the great wealth he possessed.

Then Moses, peace be upon him, demanded from Qarun the zakat on his wealth: one dinar out of every thousand dinars and one dirham out of every thousand dirhams. Qarun refused and held back, and moreover he incited the people against Moses, peace be upon him.[4]

Then he plotted a scandal to divert people away from him, for he enticed a prostitute, giving her a tray full of gold, on condition that she would accuse Moses and charge him. Moses, peace be upon him, came to address the people and explain the rulings to them, and said: "Whoever steals, we will cut off his hand; whoever commits fornication, if he is unmarried we will flog him, and if he is married we will stone him." Qarun stood up and said: "Even if it is you, O Moses?" He said: "Even if it is I."

Then the prostitute stood up and said: "He solicited me for myself." He said to her: "By Him who split the sea, you shall tell the truth." The woman trembled and confessed to what Qarun had arranged, and his deception was exposed, and the enmity between him and Moses, peace be upon him, began.

Qarun began in transgression and tyranny until Allah seized him, and concerning him these verses were revealed: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he oppressed them... 76﴾ [al-Qasas]

Al-baghy (transgression): exceeding the limit in wrongdoing, especially since he had wealth that helped him in oppression and with which he could make people serve his aims, as though he represented a centre of power among his people. Transgression is either by seizing the rights of others, or by belittling and despising them, or by insolence.

Then He mentions the basis of this transgression: ﴿And We had given him of treasures whose keys would be a burden to a band of strong men... 76﴾ [al-Qasas]

The word (mafatih, "keys") occurs as in His words: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen... 59﴾ [al-An'am]

If we say: mafatih is a plural, what is its singular? Do not say miftah, because the plural of miftah is mafatih. Rather, its singular is (miftah)[5], which is an instrument of opening like the key. It is on the pattern of (mibrad, file). The meaning is that the keys of his treasuries, if a band of men carried them, would be a burden for them. This is a metaphor for the abundance of his wealth. We say: nā'a bihi al-ḥaml, or nā'a bi al-ḥaml, when it weighed heavily upon him. We do not distinguish the light from the heavy by sight, touch, or smell, but there must be a carrying of it to sense its weight.

We have said that this sense is the sense of the muscles: a heavy load strains the muscle, so you feel its weight, unlike when you carry something light, when you barely feel its weight because of its lightness. If you try to gather weights in a narrow space, such as a (handbag), the weight will expose you, because you will strain under it.

Al-'usba (the band): they are the people who side with a principle without personal desire among them. From this is the saying of the brothers of Joseph: ﴿When they said, "Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a band (ʿuṣba)..." 8﴾ [Yusuf]

It was a word of truth that came from their mouths without intending it, because they were indeed a strong group, backing one another against Joseph and his brother, who were small, without strength or force, and they were all from one mother, while Joseph and his brother were from another mother,[6] so it is natural for the heart of Ya'qub, peace be upon him, to incline toward the weak.

It is said that the ʿuṣba is from three to ten, and the Qur'an has specified them by His saying: ﴿Indeed, I saw eleven stars... 4﴾ [Yusuf], and they were his brothers, including Binyamin; ﴿and the sun and the moon... 4﴾ [Yusuf], that is, his father and mother. From these two verses we can determine the ʿuṣba.

By this way of thinking, which rests on joining verses together, Imam 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) resolved a matter that was a difficulty for some: a man came to him and said: "I married a woman and she gave birth after six months, and it is known that a woman bears for nine months, so she must have conceived before marrying." Imam 'Ali said: "The minimum gestation is six months." The questioner said: "From where do you derive this, O Abu al-Hasan?" He said: "We derive it from His saying: ﴿And his gestation and weaning are thirty months... 15﴾ [al-Ahqaf], and in another verse He says: ﴿And mothers suckle their children for two complete years... 233﴾ [al-Baqarah]"

That is, twenty-four months, and by subtracting the twenty-four months from the thirty, the result is six months, which is the least period of gestation. Thus the verses of the Qur'an support one another and complete one another, and it is wrong to take each verse on its own and separate it from the others on the same subject.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿When his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant."⦁ 76 [al-Qasas] The prohibition here is against forbidden exultation. Al-farah (exultation) is the expansion of the soul at a matter that pleases a person. There is a difference between a matter that pleases you because it gives you enjoyment, and a matter that pleases you because it benefits you; enjoyment is not the same as benefit.

For example, a diabetic may eat sugary foods because they give him pleasure, although they are harmful to him. Thus exultation should be in what is beneficial, because Allah, exalted is He, has placed enjoyment only in what is beneficial.

So when they say to him, ﴿Do not exult...﴾ [al-Qasas, 76], they mean exultation in pleasure. Exultation should be in what is beneficial, even if it contains no pleasure, like one who takes bitter medicine that brings him recovery. For this reason He says: ﴿Say, "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice."⦁ [Yunus, 58]

And He says: ﴿On that Day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah⦁ [al-Rum, 4-5] He called it exultation because it is exultation in a beneficial thing, since the victory of the call means that the principle in which you believed and for which you fought will prevail and return to you and to the world with benefit.

From the forbidden exultation of pleasure is what the Qur'an relates: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their remaining behind, contrary to the Messenger of Allah⦁ [al-Tawbah, 81] This is the exultation of pleasure, because they disliked the Messenger of Allah and refused to go out with him, and their sitting pleased them, and his going out alone to fight displeased them.

So His saying, glorified is He, ﴿Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant⦁ 76 [al-Qasas] means the exultation of pleasure that does not look to the outcomes and consequences of things. The drinker of wine drinks it for the temporary pleasure it gives, but serious harm follows it. We hear today someone say of dancing, for example, that it is a beautiful and refined art because he finds in it some pleasure; but the condition of beautiful and refined art is that it remain beautiful, whereas if it turns afterward into ugliness and produces ugliness, as happens in dancing, it is not considered beautiful.

1 Ibn 'Abbas said: he was his cousin, and likewise said Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Simak ibn Harb, Qatadah, Malik ibn Dinar, Ibn Juraij and others, that he was a cousin of Moses, peace be upon him. Ibn Ishaq claimed that Qarun was a cousin of Moses ibn 'Imran. [Ibn Kathir in his tafsir, 3/398]
2 Na'a al-rajul bi al-ḥaml: he rose with it heavily, in effort and hardship, i.e., it weighed upon them and burdened them; this is a metaphor for the abundance of Qarun's treasures. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/290]
3 Ibn Kathir cited in his tafsir (4/266), attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim from 'Ikrimah, who said: "When the verse ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and will turn their backs⦁ [al-Qamar, 45] was revealed, 'Umar said: 'What multitude will be defeated?' i.e., what host will be overcome? 'Umar said: 'When the day of Badr came, I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leap in his armour while saying: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and will turn their backs.⦁ So on that day I understood its interpretation.'"
4 Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn 'Abbas that Moses, peace be upon him, said to Qarun: "Allah has commanded me to take the zakat." He refused, and said: "Moses wants to eat your wealth. He brought you the prayer and brought you other things, and you bore them. Will you bear that you give him your wealth?" They said: "We will not bear it. What do you advise?" He said to them: "I advise that we send to a prostitute among the prostitutes of the Children of Israel, and we send her to him so that she accuses him of having sought to lie with her." [cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 6/436]
5 al-Mifatah: a treasury. Al-Azhari said: every treasury that was for a category of things is a miftah, and mifatih: a treasure. It was said: they are treasures and storehouses. Al-Zajjaj said: it is reported that his mifatih are his treasuries. Al-Azhari said: the more likely interpretation is that his mifatih are the treasuries of his wealth, and Allah knows best what He intends. [Lisan al-'Arab, root f-t-h]
6 Ya'qub first married Leah daughter of Laban, then he married her younger sister Rachel, combining them, because that was permitted in their law. Leah bore him six sons (Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun) and one daughter (Dinah). Rachel bore him two sons: Joseph and Benjamin. His concubine Bilhah bore him two sons: Dan and Naphtali. His concubine Zilpah bore him two sons: Gad and Asher. This is what the Torah mentions in [Genesis, chapter 35:23–26].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 28, verse 77:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{And seek, in what Allah has given you, the Abode of the Hereafter, and do not forget your portion of this world. And do good as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the earth. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters.} (28:77)

The meaning of ﴿And seek...﴾ (77): that is, seek, ﴿in what Allah has given you﴾ (77) of the provision He has bestowed upon you, ﴿the Abode of the Hereafter﴾ (77). For if you seek with the provision Allah has given you the life of this world, it will perish along with you in this world. But if you give it up for the Hereafter, He will preserve for you a lasting bounty that does not cease.

When you love the bounties of this world, single them out and cling to them, know that your death will not give you respite: either you will lose this bounty through death, or it will be lost to you when you become poor. Therefore: if you are a lover and devotee of wealth, and want it to remain in your possession, then transfer it to the Abode that endures, so that it will remain in your embrace forever as a lasting bounty that never leaves you. So hasten, then, and let it precede you to the Hereafter.

In the noble hadith, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked his mother of the believers, ʿĀʾishah, about the sheep that had been sent to him as a gift, she said after she had given it in charity: "Nothing is left except its shoulder." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, everything is left except its shoulder."(1)

And he (ﷺ) said: "None of your wealth is yours except what you eat and consume, or wear and wear out, or give in charity and thereby preserve."(2)

Thus it was that people of resolve, when a beggar came to one of them, would say to him: "Welcome to the one who comes carrying my provision to the Hereafter without a fee."

Imam ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) was approached by a man who asked him: "Am I among the people of this world, or among the people of the Hereafter?" He said: "The answer to this question is not with me, but with you, and you are the judge in this matter. If someone comes to you whom you are accustomed to giving to, and someone comes to you whom you are accustomed to taking from, and if you brighten up for the one who gives, then you are of the people of this world; but if you brighten up for the one who asks you and takes from you, then you are of the people of the Hereafter. For a person loves whoever makes what he loves flourish for him. So if you love this world, the one who gives you will delight you; and if you love the Hereafter, the one who takes from you will delight you."

Since our Lord, mighty and majestic, enjoins us to seek the Hereafter, this does not mean that we should abandon this world: ﴿and do not forget your portion of this world﴾ (77). Yet some people take this verse as evidence for immersion in the world and its pleasures.

When we reflect on ﴿do not forget your portion of this world﴾ (77), we understand that the wise person should look upon this world as not deserving of concern, but his Lord turned his attention to it so that he might take from it what the movement of his life requires.

So the meaning is: I should have forgotten it, but Allah reminded me of it.

The people of knowledge have a subtle insight on this question. They say: your portion of a thing is what reaches you of it, not in the sense of separation but in the sense of attachment and continuance. Accordingly, your portion of this world is the good deed that remains for you, stays with you, and accompanies you beyond this world into the Hereafter. It is as if your portion of this world flows into your portion of the Hereafter, so that your worldly life serves your Hereafter.

Or the meaning may be directed at the miser who withholds from himself, so that his Lord reminds him: ﴿and do not forget your portion of this world﴾ (77), that is: take from it the measure that helps you with the affair of the Hereafter. Therefore they said about this world: it is too important to be forgotten, because it is the means to the Hereafter, and too trivial to be an end, because beyond it there is another end that is more enduring and more lasting.(3)

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾ (77). The Truth, glorified is He, wants His creatures to take on His character, as has come in the report: "Take on the characteristics of Allah."

Just as Allah has been good to you, be good to people; and just as you wish Allah to forgive you, forgive others their wrongdoing: ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ (24:22)

As long as your Lord gives to you, you must give without fear of poverty, for Allah, exalted is He, is the One who brought you into existence; therefore He has undertaken your sustenance, your upbringing, and your care. So when you see one who is unable to earn, whom his Lord has placed in this condition for a wisdom, and he extends his hand to you, know that he extends it to Allah, and that you are a conduit on behalf of Allah, exalted is He.

We observe this meaning in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?﴾ (57:11)

He called charity a loan to Allah. Why? Because this servant is My servant, and it is incumbent upon Me to provide for him, and I have tested him for a wisdom with Me, so that no one thinks the matter is inherent in him and takes a lesson from it for others. So who, then, will lend to Me to meet the need of your brother?

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah lends﴾ (57:11), although He is the Bestower; this is because He wanted to honour your ownership, and to honour your benefit and your striving. It is like a father who wants to have one of his sons undergo a surgical operation, for example, while he is poor and his brothers are rich, so he says to his children: "Lend me from your wealth so that I may have surgery done for your brother, and I will repay you this loan."

In the noble hadith, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon his daughter Fāṭimah (may Allah be pleased with her) and found her polishing a dirham. He asked her: "What are you doing with it?" She said: "I am polishing it." He said: "Why?" She said: "Because I intended to give it in charity, and I know that it falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the poor."

So: wealth is Allah's wealth, and you are a conduit on behalf of Allah, exalted is He.

Some orientalists paused at this question, because they read the verses and hadiths with a mere superficial, unthinking reading, and so they imagine that they contradict each other. They said here: Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, and He will multiply it for him﴾ (57:11)

And He said in another place: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ (6:160). And in the noble hadith: "It is written on the gate of Paradise: charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan eighteenfold."(4)

So the apparent sense of the hadith differs from the noble verse, in their view, because they do not possess the Arabic linguistic faculty for receiving the Qur'anic exposition. Upon reflection on the verses and hadiths, we find that they agree that a good deed or a charity is rewarded tenfold. The apparent difference lies in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and He will multiply it for him﴾ (57:11) and the Prophet's saying (ﷺ): "and a loan eighteenfold."

There is no real contradiction between them. When a person gives a dirham in charity, for example, Allah gives him ten in return, including the dirham he gave; so it is as if He has given him nine, and when the nine are multiplied, they become eighteen.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾ (77). Corruption comes from departing from the way of Allah. If you alter it, you have corrupted it. Corruption occurs in the material realm just as it occurs in the method and in matters of meaning. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do not corrupt the earth after its reformation﴾ (7:56).

The Truth, glorified is He, created everything in the form of goodness to bring happiness to His creatures, so do not intend to it and corrupt it. Among this goodness is the method, indeed the method, which is the foundation of spiritual life, takes precedence over the foundation of material life.

So: be courteous with the cosmos around you. If you cannot make it better, then at least leave it as it is without corrupting it. We have given an example of this: a well of water, which you may deliberately fill in, or around which you may build a wall to protect it.

These are five matters by which the people of Qarun addressed him in counsel. Some were commands and some prohibitions. They must have found in him what contradicted them. They must have found him insolent and arrogant, proud of his wealth, so they said to him: ﴿Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾ (76).

They found that he had forgotten his portion of this world, not provisioning himself from it for the Hereafter, so they said to him: ﴿and do not forget your portion of this world﴾ (77). They found him stingy toward himself, not spending in goodness, so they said to him: ﴿and do good as Allah has done good to you﴾ (77), that is: extend your blessing to others as Allah's blessing has extended to you. And so on: they did not command him a command, nor forbid him a prohibition, except that he was acting contrary to it; otherwise they would not have commanded him or forbidden him.

1 Narrated by Aḥmad in his Musnad (6/50) and al-Tirmidhī in his Sunan (2470), from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her). al-Tirmidhī said: "This is a ṣaḥīḥ hadith."
2 Narrated by Aḥmad in his Musnad (4/24, 26), Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (2958), and al-Tirmidhī in his Sunan (2342), who authenticated it.
3 al-Qurṭubī said in his tafsir (7/5201): "His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not forget your portion of this world﴾ (77) — there is difference of opinion on it. Ibn ʿAbbās and the majority said: do not waste your life by not doing righteous deeds in your world, since the Hereafter is only attained by works; a person's portion is his life and his righteous deed in it, so the address on this interpretation is a severe admonition. Al-Ḥasan and Qatādah said: its meaning is: do not waste your share of your world through your enjoyment of what is lawful and seeking it, and your looking to the outcome of your world. So the address on this interpretation contains some gentleness toward him and the rectification of the matter he desires; this is what must be used with the one being admonished, lest he flee from severity, as Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said."
4 On the authority of Abū Umāmah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "A man entered Paradise and saw written on its gate: charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan eighteenfold." Cited by al-Haythamī in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid (4/126), attributed to al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr, and he said: "In it is ʿUtbah ibn Ḥumayd, who was deemed reliable by Ibn Ḥibbān and others, but in whom there is weakness."
And on the authority of Anas ibn Mālik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw written on the gate of Paradise: charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan eighteen. I said to Jibrīl: why is a loan better than charity? He said: because the one who asks, asks when he has it, while the one who borrows borrows only out of need." Narrated by Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah (8/333).
5 al-Ashar: insolence, i.e. al-biṭar. It is said: it is an intensified form of biṭar. Biṭar: excessive pride in blessings, so one who is biṭar has not given thanks for them. [Lisān al-ʿArab, entries: ashara, biṭara]

Then Qarun, responding to these five questions that his people put to him, says:

{He said: "I have only been given it on account of knowledge that I possess. Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him in might and greater in number? And the guilty will not be asked about their sins."} (28:78)

But what is the purpose of this response, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge that I possess" (28:78), to the five demands they made of him? It is as if he is saying to them: "This is none of your concern, for the One who gave me the wealth knew that I am worthy of it and that I deserve it; therefore He entrusted it to me, and I have no need of your advice."

Or the meaning may be: "I have only been given it on account of knowledge that I possess" (28:78), i.e., through my own effort and my practice of the work that brings in this wealth. Qarun was renowned for his beautiful voice in reciting the Torah, and he was a memorizer of it.

He was also handsome, and at a high level of knowledge of the rulings of the Torah.

It is strange that he should have all this knowledge and yet say, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge that I possess" (28:78), and not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him, and greater in wealth and number.

"Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him in might and greater in number" (28:78). How, then, did this matter escape him, given his knowledge of the Torah?

The meaning of "Did he not know" (28:78) is: among what he knew were people from generations who had more wealth than him, whom Allah seized, and they were nations, not individuals. The word "jam'an" (in multitude / in number, 28:78) may be a verbal noun meaning "the gathering of wealth," or a noun for a group, meaning that he had a band of followers.

After that, He, glorified is He, said: "And the guilty will not be asked about their sins" (28:78). The sign that they will not be questioned is that Allah, exalted is He, seizes them without warning, seizing them unawares. He will not say to Qarun: "You did such-and-such, and I will do such-and-such to you, and I will cause the earth to swallow you and your home." Your deeds are known to you, and the preceding circumstances are sufficient for the punishment to surprise you.

Thus he should expect that the sinking into the earth and the punishment may come to him at any time. Therefore, We will not question them, nor will We conduct with them an investigation like that of the public prosecution or the police, where there is no benefit in questioning them, and for them there is nothing with Us but punishment.

After all of this, and after his people had advised him, Qarun remained arrogant and insolent. He did not heed the counsel nor refrain; rather he remained exultant, transgressing and causing corruption. The Qur'an narrates about him:

{So he went forth before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the life of this world said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune."79}

We have said that Qarun was naturally wealthy and of high standing, handsome of voice and appearance, of great numbers and abundant wealth. So how much more so when you add to all this that he went out in his adornment, in a great procession and in splendour, ﴿So he went forth before his people in his adornment..79﴾ [Al-Qasas]

The scholars have much to say (1) about this adornment in which Qarun went out. It is said that there were a thousand female slaves of such and such attributes, and a thousand horses, etc., so that people were dazzled by him and by his adornment. Indeed, they were divided because of him into two groups: a group who were seduced by him, whom the glitter of blessing, the adornment, the pride and the luxury of life captivated, and who cast their eyes upon the pleasure of the world that he possessed.

And concerning these the Exalted says: ﴿Those who desired the life of this world said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune."79﴾ [Al-Qasas] The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, addressed His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saying: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them, the flower of the life of this world..131﴾ [Ta-Ha]

The meaning is: do not look at what is in the hand of others, and respect the decree of Allah concerning His creation. Know that if you rejoice in the blessing that is with another, its good comes to you, knocking at your door, and it serves you as though it were with you; but if you dislike it and envy him for it, it turns away from you and you are deprived of its benefit, because a blessing loves its possessor more than he loves it. So how would it come to you when you dislike it being with another?

Therefore, among the attributes of the believer is that he loves for his brother good as he loves it for himself. When you do not love a blessing in the hand of another, what is his fault? It is as if you are objecting to the decree of Allah concerning him. And as long as you have turned away and objected to the decree of the Bestower, it is inevitable that He will deprive you of it.

Therefore He, glorified be He, says elsewhere: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others..32﴾ [An-Nisa']

Because each of you has a task and a role in life, and each of you has his talents and distinctions by which he is distinguished from others. It must be that in you are qualities better than those of the one you envy, but you are heedless of them and not attentive to them.

We have previously said that the Truth, glorified be He, has distributed the causes of His bounty among His creation, because we are all equal before Allah, and He, glorified be He, has taken neither a consort nor a son. Therefore we said that the sum of the talents of each individual equals the sum of the talents of another. You may surpass me in one quality, and I surpass you in another: this one is distinguished by intelligence, that one by health, another by knowledge, another by forbearance, etc.

Because the movement of life requires all these capacities, by them life is completed, and it is not possible that all these virtues be available to one person who performs all the tasks. Rather, if you excel in your work and perfect your duty, then to you is gratitude.

It is strange that you do not benefit from your own excellence while others benefit from it. Among this is their saying, for example: "The carpenter's door is loose" (Bab al-najjar mukhala'). Why does he not make a door for himself, being a carpenter? They say: because it is the only door for which he does not charge a fee.

So: when you find another excelling in something, do not harbour resentment against him, for his excellence will return to benefit you. We give a simple example of this: when you hold the scissors in your right hand to cut the nails of the left hand, you find that the right hand, because it is supple and easy in movement, cuts the nails of the left precisely; but when the left cuts the nails of the right, it does not give you the same skill that the right had.

So: the goodness of the right hand extends to the left and benefits it.

Likewise, when you see your brother excel in something or do well in its making, praise God, for his goodness and excellence will return to you, though it may not return to him. So do not envy him, and do not harbour resentment against him; rather pray for him for more, for you will benefit from him one day.

But what did the people of this world say, who were dazzled by the adornment of Qarun? They said: ﴿Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune.79﴾ [Al-Qasas] That is: as we say, "his luck is a bomb" (hazzuhu bamb); because these people care only for the affair of the world, its pleasures and its ornament. But the people of knowledge and of insight have a different opinion and a farther view of matters; therefore they replied to them:

{And those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness; and none is granted it except the patient.80}

1 Qatada said: he went out on four thousand beasts, upon which were red garments, among them a thousand white mules upon which were red saddle-cloths. [Reported by Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim] – Ibn Jurayj said: he went out on a grey mule upon which was crimson, and with him three hundred female slaves on grey mules, upon whom were red garments. [Reported by Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim]. Al-Suyuti cited these narrations and others in [al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi'l-Ma'thur 6/441].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 28, verse 80:

Allah, blessed and exalted, would not leave the people of this world and the people of falsehood to cast doubt among people concerning the decree of Allah and to rebel against His allotment, to the point of disbelief and heresy. And Allah, glorified is He, never leaves mankind without people of truth who balance the scale of life's movement. As the saying goes: "He who made the truth a bitter pill has never left a generation without people of truth."

Since Allah, exalted is He, said of the first group: ﴿And those who desire the life of this world... 79﴾ [al-Qasas], they see nothing beyond it and aspire to nothing further than it. And He said of the other: ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said... 80﴾ [al-Qasas]. This means that the people of this world are superficial; they did not possess knowledge that would benefit them. Therefore they fell into this dilemma from which the people of knowledge were saved, when they made a comparison between the desire for the world and the desire for the Hereafter.

As we have said previously: the age of the world, in relation to you, should not be measured from Adam to the Hour; your own life within it is a timed life that must come to an end. So the intelligent person is the one who chooses the enduring over the perishing. For this reason the people of the world said: ﴿Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given... 79﴾ [al-Qasas].

As for the people of knowledge and insight, they replied to them: ﴿Woe to you... 80﴾ [al-Qasas]. That is: woe to you because of this superficial thinking. And wishing for what Qarun has means woe and ruin for you, because you envied people, harboured spite against them, and objected to Allah's decrees in His creation.

You deserve ruin for this. Therefore Allah said of them in another place: ﴿But most of mankind do not know. They know an outward appearance of the worldly life... 6-7﴾ [al-Rum].

That is: they do not know the reality of things, and had they known, they would not have said this statement or made this wish.

Then the people of knowledge and insight draw the attention of the people of the world and direct them to the right course: ﴿The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds... 80﴾ [al-Qasas]. That is: Allah's reward is better than the world and than what Qarun has. How can you wish for what he has, when you denounced his conduct and forbade him from it, and did not approve of it?

As for the meaning of ﴿But none is granted it except the patient... 80﴾ [al-Qasas]: that is, faith, righteous deeds and guidance are granted only to the one who turns toward the work of the Hereafter and prefers it over the world. That is, he grasps the matter of knowledge of realities, and apparent appearances do not deceive him. This is not found, nor is one granted success in it, except by the patient, as He, glorified is He, said in another verse: ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune. 35﴾ [Fussilat].

Patience (al-sabr) is enduring what is outwardly painful but which brings bliss inwardly. It has stages. Allah has obligated us to acts of obedience, which contain commands, and has obligated us to stay away from acts of disobedience, which contain prohibitions, and He has sent down upon us decrees that our souls may not find pleasant. These are three stages.

Acts of obedience are heavy and burdensome on the soul. Therefore He, exalted is He, says of prayer: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humble... 45﴾ [al-Baqarah]. There are various motives that turn you away from prayer and try to keep you from it, so you find laziness and heaviness when you stand for prayer.

Read His saying, addressing His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning prayer: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it... 132﴾ [Ta-Ha]. This is evidence that it is hard and burdensome on the soul, but if you get accustomed to it, and the soul becomes familiar with it, it becomes the most beloved of things to you, the lightest on your self, and indeed the coolness of your eyes.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, teaches us this lesson in his saying to his muezzin Bilal: "Give us rest through it, O Bilal" (1), not "Relieve us of it," which is the saying our present condition speaks.

He also, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "And the coolness of my eyes has been made in prayer" (2). He singled out prayer from among the other acts of worship, because it recurs five times a day; it accompanies the believer throughout his day and night, unlike the other pillars, some of which occur once a year or once in a lifetime.

This is the first type of patience: patience upon the hardship of obedience.

The second: patience against the desire of sin. Do not forget that the first patience you encounter in life is to be patient with yourself. Therefore the poet (3) says:

"If you wish to borrow money to spend
on the desires of the soul in a time of hardship,
then let your soul be the one to spend from the treasure of its patience,
granting you respite until the hour of ease.
If you do so, you will be rich; and if it refuses,
then every refuser after that has a broad excuse."

So instead of borrowing to satisfy a hasty desire of the soul, it is better for you to be patient until you find ease and facility. Your patience with yourself is easier than the patience of people with you. If your soul does not accommodate you, then no one has any excuse after that for denying you.

The third: patience with painful decrees whose wisdom you do not perceive. Since decrees come from a Wise One, and their executor upon you is your Lord, there must be wisdom in them concerning you. So take the matter of decree according to the wisdom of the one who executes it upon you. He, glorified is He, is your Lord, not your enemy; you are His servant and His creation. Have you not read the Prophet's saying in the noble hadith: "All creation is the dependents of Allah, and the most beloved of them to Him is the most merciful to His dependents" (4)?

Thus, when painful decrees befall you, it is sufficient for your patience that you know them to be the wisdom of Allah, and sufficient that the one who executes them upon you is your Lord. If painful decrees come because of your own shortcoming, then blame no one but yourself, like the student who neglects his lessons and is lazy, and so fails the examination; the failure is the result of his neglect and laziness.

As for the one who studies, strives, and approaches the examination full of hope, and then a car strikes him on the road, preventing him from sitting his exam, this is the painful decree that has wisdom.
